items.title: UNDP–Generali MSME Insurance Innovation Challenge (India)
items.amount: Up to US$40,000 (~₹35 lakh) each, max 3 winners
items.summary: UNDP India and Generali Central are funding up to three insurance solutions that make cover affordable and relevant for Indian MSMEs, their workers and gig workers. It is aimed at existing solutions with traction, not fresh ideas; winners get up to US$40,000 each to develop or scale.
eligibility: Existing solutions with demonstrated traction (not idea-stage concepts)
Solution must strengthen MSME resilience — e.g. health, disability, life, business-interruption, asset-loss or liability cover
Priority areas: affordable cover for MSMEs and employees, tech-enabled or embedded insurance, new distribution channels, and products for gig workers
Solutions that advance young entrepreneurs and women are prioritised
Full criteria are in the challenge FAQ linked from the UNDP call page
benefits: Award of up to US$40,000 per winning solution to develop or scale it
Up to three winners, announced February 2027
Access to UNDP and Generali Central expertise and networks
items.note: Applications close 10 December 2026 via the online form linked as 'Apply here' on the UNDP call page (closing time not stated). Read the FAQ for formal eligibility before applying; the applicant webinar (27 Oct) has already happened. Earlier reports cited 20 Nov — the official page now shows 10 Dec.

items.title: Grassroot Innovation Programme 2026
items.summary: Grant for grassroots innovators in Karnataka building solutions to local, community-level problems.
eligibility: Innovators based in Karnataka
benefits: Grant up to ₹4 lakh
items.note: Deadline 23 Nov 2026, 5 PM. Link is a listing page — confirm on the KITS portal.

items.title: BE Hub Udaan — Accelerator Cohort 1
items.summary: 12-week acceleration programme for early-stage deep-tech and tech-led startups. Only 5–6 startups selected; starts 23 Nov 2026.
eligibility: Early-stage founders building deep-tech or tech-led startups
benefits: Idea and business-model validation
Industry network access
Growth preparation
items.note: Deadline 18 Nov 2026.

items.title: Techstars Accelerators 2027 (incl. Anywhere / London)
items.summary: 3-month accelerator; the remote 'Anywhere' and London programmes accept global founders, including from India. Programme starts 8 Mar 2027.
eligibility: Early-stage startups, any sector
benefits: USD 220K investment
Mentor network and demo day
items.note: Applications close 18 Nov 2026.

items.title: Ye! Youth Ecopreneurs Programme (YECO) 2026/27
items.summary: Global programme for young green entrepreneurs building land-restoration and environmental businesses.
eligibility: Founder / co-founder / CEO under 35 at the deadline
Green business with a scalable solution
benefits: Share of USD 100K prizes
All-expenses-paid trip to an international conference
Acceleration support
items.note: Deadline 22 Nov 2026. Link is a listing page — confirm on ITC's Ye! site.

items.title: NIDHI-PRAYAS
items.summary: Prototype grant for innovators turning an idea into a working proof-of-concept, routed through DST-approved PRAYAS incubators.
eligibility: Individual innovators or early teams
Apply through a PRAYAS centre (incubator)
benefits: Up to ₹10 lakh for prototyping
Incubator lab and mentoring access
items.note: Rolling/periodic calls via individual PRAYAS centres.

items.title: NIDHI Seed Support System (NIDHI-SSS)
items.summary: Seed support for startups incubated at DST-backed TBIs, typically via convertible or equity-linked instruments.
eligibility: Incubated at a DST-supported TBI
Indian startup with a tech product
benefits: Seed funding up to ₹1 Cr
items.note: Apply through your incubator; each TBI runs its own window.

items.title: BIRAC Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG)
items.summary: BIRAC's flagship early-stage grant to take biotech ideas to proof-of-concept, managed through partner bio-incubators.
eligibility: Biotech / life-science innovation
Individuals or startups (DPIIT/company as per call)
benefits: Grant up to ₹50 lakh over ~18 months
Mentoring by BIG partners
items.note: Two calls a year; watch BIRAC's call-for-proposals page.

items.title: RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubation
items.summary: Grant-in-aid for agri and allied startups through RKVY-RAFTAAR agribusiness incubators (R-ABIs) across India.
eligibility: Agriculture / allied-sector startups
Selected through an R-ABI cohort
benefits: Pre-seed up to ₹5 lakh
Seed up to ₹25 lakh
Two-month incubation training
items.note: Cohort calls by individual R-ABIs (IARI Pusa, MANAGE, etc.).

items.title: iDEX — Innovations for Defence Excellence
items.summary: Defence India Startup Challenges (DISC) and open challenges where startups solve problem statements from the armed forces.
eligibility: Indian startups / MSMEs / individual innovators
Solution to a published defence problem statement
benefits: Grant up to ₹1.5 Cr
Path to procurement by the armed forces
items.note: New DISC rounds are released periodically.

items.title: MSME Innovative Scheme (Incubation)
items.org: Ministry of MSME via Host Institutes
items.summary: Funding to develop and nurture ideas into prototypes through approved Host Institutes (incubators).
eligibility: Individual innovators / MSMEs
Apply via an approved Host Institute
benefits: Up to ₹15 lakh per idea
items.note: Rolling via the MSME Innovative portal.

items.title: Kerala Startup Mission Grants (Idea → Scale-up)
items.summary: Stage-wise grants: Idea (₹3L), Productization (₹7L; ₹12L for women/transgender founders), Market Acceleration (₹10L), Scale-up (₹15L).
eligibility: Startups registered with KSUM / operating in Kerala
benefits: Stage-based equity-free grants
items.note: Periodic calls; check KSUM schemes page.

items.title: StartinUP Incentives (UP Startup Policy 2026)
items.amount: ₹20K/month for 2 yrs + up to ₹10L prototype + up to ₹15L seed
items.summary: Under UP Startup Policy 2026: sustenance allowance, a one-time prototype grant and seed capital for StartinUP-registered startups, plus free incubation for up to two years.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Registered and recognised on the StartinUP portal (Uttar Pradesh)
benefits: Sustenance allowance ₹20,000/month for 2 years
Prototype grant up to ₹10 lakh
Seed capital up to ₹15 lakh
Free incubation up to 2 years at recognised incubators/CoEs
items.note: Rolling. Detailed operational guidelines are published on the UP Startup Mission portal.

items.title: UP Startup Policy 2026 — Matching Grant
items.summary: Matches 50% of external capital raised by UP-recognised startups, capped at ₹5 crore.
eligibility: UP state-recognised startup
Prior fundraise of at least ₹2 crore
benefits: Matching grant up to ₹5 Cr
items.note: Open year-round. Confirm operational guidelines on the portal.

items.title: UP Grand Challenges Grant
items.summary: Open competitive calls under UP Startup Policy 2026; scaling-stage winners receive grant-in-aid.
eligibility: UP state-recognised startup
Scaling stage
benefits: Grant-in-aid up to ₹3 Cr
items.note: Challenges announced periodically.

items.title: Student Startup & Innovation Policy (SSIP 2.0)
items.summary: Proof-of-concept support for student and recent-graduate innovators in Gujarat institutions.
eligibility: Students / recent grads of Gujarat institutions
benefits: PoC grant up to ₹2.5 lakh
items.note: Rolling via institute SSIP cells.

items.title: i-Hub Gujarat — Startup Srujan
items.summary: Seed support (S4) under Gujarat's SSIP 2.0, implemented by i-Hub, for student and early-stage innovators.
eligibility: Student / young innovators from Gujarat's education ecosystem (under 35)
benefits: Grant ₹2.5L–₹10L
Incubation at i-Hub Ahmedabad
items.note: Rolling.

items.title: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
items.amount: Collateral-free loans, guarantee cover up to ₹20 crore
items.summary: Government guarantee on loans and venture debt from banks, NBFCs and AIF debt funds to DPIIT startups, so lenders need no collateral.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup
Stable revenue / not in default
benefits: Collateral-free debt
Guarantee cover up to ₹20 Cr per borrower
items.note: Apply through member lending institutions.

items.title: Technology Development Board — Funding
items.summary: Low-interest loans and equity support to commercialise indigenous technology; also runs bilateral calls (e.g. India–Finland).
eligibility: Indian company commercialising a technology
benefits: Soft loans at concessional interest
Equity / grant in select calls
items.note: Rolling applications plus periodic calls.

items.title: 100Unicorns Accelerator VC
items.summary: Accelerator VC giving seed funding and hands-on support to early-stage Indian startups from idea to angel stage.
eligibility: Early-stage Indian startups
benefits: Seed cheque
Mentoring and follow-on network
items.note: Always open.

items.title: Zero Shot Fund
items.summary: USD 100M fund backing AI-native founders in robotics, energy, automation, infrastructure, security and observability. No deck needed to start a conversation.
eligibility: Building an AI-native company
benefits: USD 1M–4M cheque
items.note: Rolling. Link is a listing page — find the fund's own apply form.

items.title: First in the World Challenge Grants 2026
items.amount: Up to ₹8 Cr (staged: ₹1 Cr / ₹4 Cr / ₹8 Cr)
items.summary: ICMR's high-risk, high-reward call for health technologies that have never been attempted anywhere in the world — new vaccines, drugs, diagnostics or interventions — funded in milestone-linked stages up to ₹8 crore.
eligibility: Indian startups, MSMEs and industry can apply alongside academic and research institutions
Government medical colleges, INIs, ICMR institutes, universities and recognised R&D labs
Private institutions and NGOs registered with DSIR as research organisations (NGOs must also be on NITI Aayog's DARPAN portal)
Each proposal needs one Principal Investigator plus at least one Co-PI from the same institution
Idea must be genuinely first-of-its-kind globally; incremental improvements are rejected
benefits: Proof-of-concept stage: up to ₹1 Cr over 2 years
Prototype stage: up to ₹4 Cr over 3 years
Final product/model stage: up to ₹8 Cr over 4 years
Non-dilutive funding released against deliverables, with a path to the next stage
items.note: Submit only on the ICMR e-PMS portal (epms.icmr.org.in) by 30 Nov 2026, 5:30 PM IST; results expected 31 Dec 2026. Incomplete proposals are rejected before review. Selected teams must later provide an institutional undertaking, ethics (IEC) approval where relevant, and bank details.

items.title: Hello Tomorrow Global Challenge 2026–27
items.amount: €200K investment for the top pitch + in-kind prizes
items.summary: Free-to-enter global deep-tech competition with 12 tracks; around 800 startups become Deep Tech Pioneers, about 90 finalists pitch at the Amsterdam summit in June 2027, and the winner pitch carries a €200K investment from DeepBright Ventures.
eligibility: Deep-tech startups built on new technology, a scientific discovery or complex engineering
Stage: proof of concept or prototype up to Series B
Team of at least two people
Not a subsidiary or spin-off of an existing company
Market application expected within 15 years; incorporation not needed to apply
benefits: Deep Tech Pioneer status and Investor Day meetings with 300+ VCs and CVCs
Finalists pitch for a €200K investment from DeepBright Ventures
Track-winner coaching and investor, partner and customer introductions
Corporate-track pitching slots and prizes
items.note: Applications close 30 Nov 2026 and are free. Pioneers are notified late Jan–early Feb 2027; finalists in mid-March. Summit tickets need a refundable €99 deposit, and travel and accommodation to Amsterdam are not covered. Prize funds are only paid once the startup is incorporated.

items.title: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST)
items.org: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, managed by IFCI Venture Capital Funds
items.summary: A ₹50 crore government-anchored fund that backs Scheduled Tribe-owned businesses and startups, mainly through convertible or non-convertible debentures, with limited equity for innovative tech startups.
eligibility: Company at least 51% owned and managed by Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs
Ownership and control held for 6 months (up to ₹50 lakh) or 12 months (above ₹50 lakh)
Manufacturing, services or allied sectors, including TBI-incubated startups; projects must create assets
A new company can qualify as successor to an eligible proprietorship, partnership, OPC or LLP
Documentary proof of ST status required; women-led ventures preferred for at least 30% of support
benefits: ₹10 lakh to ₹5 crore, capped at twice the company's net worth
TBI-selected tech projects: up to ₹10 lakh a year for 3 years
Instruments include CCDs, OCDs and NCDs; equity up to 49% for innovative tech startups
Government-anchored capital with screening via NSTFDC
items.note: Rolling scheme with no fixed closing date. Funding is mostly debt-style debentures, so expect repayment or conversion terms; assistance is limited to twice your net worth. Applications are sourced through NSTFDC and IFCI Venture — contact them for the current application route.

items.title: National Startup Awards 6.0 (2026)
items.org: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Startup India)
items.summary: The government's flagship startup awards are back with a much bigger purse: ₹25 lakh for the winner in each of 20 sector categories and two special categories, up from ₹10 lakh last edition. A separate ₹25 lakh pool covers school and college student innovators.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup (private limited company, registered partnership or LLP)
Not more than 10 years old from the date of incorporation
Annual turnover never above ₹100 crore in any financial year
Not under insolvency proceedings; past NSA winners cannot re-apply
Student Innovator track: school/college students (individual or team of up to 4) with a prototype, MVP or proof of concept; DPIIT recognition not needed
benefits: ₹25 lakh cash prize per winning category (20 sectoral + Women-Led Startup of the Year + North-East Startup Excellence)
Student track prizes from ₹2 lakh to ₹6 lakh across four age groups
Mentoring, investor connects, market access and corporate tie-ups
National visibility and priority at DPIIT-backed startup events in India and abroad
items.note: Applications opened 27 Oct 2026 and close 20 Nov 2026 per DPIIT's launch announcement (one aggregator shows 30 Nov — treat 20 Nov as the safe date). Keep your DPIIT certificate and recent financial statements ready; check the portal for the full category rules and how many categories you may enter.

items.title: Start Up Energy Transition (SET) Award 2027
items.summary: A long-running global competition for energy and climate-tech startups, run by Germany's national energy agency. Five category winners take equity-free prize money, and finalists get a stage at the SET Tech Festival in Berlin in front of investors and corporates.
eligibility: Company founded in August 2016 or later, registered or in the process of registering
Past the idea stage with at least a proof of concept
Must have a client, an institutional/corporate partner, or a working prototype (hardware generally TRL 4+)
Apply to only one of the five categories; full application and attachments in English
Open to startups worldwide, including India
benefits: €10,000 equity-free prize for each category winner
Showcase and networking at the SET Tech Festival in Berlin
Media visibility through dena's international network
Introductions to energy-sector investors and corporate partners
items.note: Closes 30 Nov 2026 (Central European time — submit by the evening of 30 Nov IST to be safe). Late or partially completed applications are rejected. Categories: Clean Energy & Storage; Digital Energy, Markets & Economy; Buildings & Construction; Industry & Value Chains; Mobility & Transportation. No application fee mentioned.

items.title: Telangana Innovation Startup Challenge (TISC) 2026
items.summary: Telangana is asking startups to solve seven concrete public-sector problems — led by low-cost solar irrigation for deep borewells — with the reward being paid government pilots that can turn into long-term procurement contracts. Shortlisted teams will be showcased at the Invest Telangana Global Summit in December 2026.
eligibility: Startups, innovators, researchers, technology firms and academic institutions
Applicants from anywhere in India (and international innovation centres) may apply
Solution must address one of the seven listed problem statements
Judged on problem relevance, originality, technology readiness, team capability and impact
benefits: Pilot deployment with Telangana government departments
Route to long-term government procurement contracts, subject to pilot results
Showcase slot at the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 (Bharat Future City, December)
Direct engagement with state officials on real-world problems
items.note: Deadline 30 Nov 2026. The seven challenges: solar irrigation pumps/retrofit kits for deep borewells (~30% cheaper, theft-resistant panels, tamper-proof metering); rapid food-adulteration testing for hostels; satellite monitoring of lake and land encroachment; automated pothole mapping and repair; needle-free anaemia screening; AI-based Telugu reading assessment; satellite/app-based crop mapping. No cash prize announced — the value is the pilot and contract pathway.

items.title: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
items.amount: Up to USD 5K Azure credits + prizes
items.summary: Microsoft's global AI startup competition, now run as seven categories including a dedicated Student Startup track. Teams build on Microsoft Cloud and AI, and category winners and finalists advance to a World Championship.
eligibility: Every team member must be at least 18 and register individually; teams of up to four
The startup must be a registered legal entity founded on or after 2 November 2024
Must not have raised Series C or later funding; past Imagine Cup winners cannot re-enter
Not based in or operating from US-sanctioned regions (India is eligible)
Student-led startups can enter the Student Startup category
benefits: Up to USD 5,000 in Azure credits for registered teams to build an MVP
Category winner and Top 20 Startup recognition
Finalists and the Student Prize winner pitch at the World Championship
Visibility with Microsoft for Startups and its partner network
items.note: Submissions close 11:59 pm US Central Time on 28 Feb 2027 (about 11:29 am IST on 1 Mar). You cannot edit after submitting. Cash prize amounts are not listed on the official FAQ, and the Official Rules override the FAQ, so read them before entering.

items.title: MedTech Innovator 2027 Accelerator
items.amount: Share of USD 700K+ prizes (top prize USD 350K)
items.summary: A five-month, mentor-led accelerator for medical device, diagnostics and digital health companies that ends in a public prize competition. Non-US startups, including Indian ones, are welcome as long as they plan to enter the US market.
eligibility: Building a medical device, diagnostic or digital health product
Early to mid-stage, with clinical validation in progress or on the horizon
A founder or C-suite leader must commit to the full five-month programme
Companies outside the US can apply but need a clear US market strategy
No fee to apply
benefits: Mentor matching with industry leaders and access to investors
Early-stage track competes for USD 350K and mid-stage track for USD 250K at the finals, plus extra awards
Showcase at The MedTech Conference
Partner resources and in-kind services through the programme
items.note: Applications close 1 Dec 2026 (US time, so submit by 30 Nov in India to be safe). Applying is free, but selected companies pay a USD 15,000 programme fee in cash or as a USD 50K SAFE. Scholarships exist, and some specialty tracks require a USD 50K SAFE. Expect US travel for in-person events.

items.title: BioTools Innovator 2027 Accelerator
items.amount: Up to USD 250K grand prize (USD 300K+ pool)
items.summary: A non-profit accelerator and prize competition for companies building life science research tools, diagnostics, software and services used by drug developers. Startups headquartered anywhere, including India, can apply if they have a US go-to-market plan.
eligibility: Life science tools, diagnostics, software or services for drug developers (drug, biologic, cell and gene therapy developers are out of scope)
Pre-seed to Series B, with a prototype and proof of concept in hand or close to it
Raised no more than USD 25M in equity
International companies welcome with a clear US market strategy
Must be incorporated before the programme starts and attend two mandatory in-person events
benefits: USD 250K for the finals winner, USD 25K for each of up to four finalists and USD 10K for the best video
Mentorship from corporate partners, workshops and investor pitching
A BARDA-backed VANGUARD track for up to ten biotools startups, with its programme fee fully covered
items.note: Closes 1 Dec 2026; no closing time is published, so submit a few days early. No application fee, but accepted companies pay USD 15,000 (cash, two instalments, or a USD 50K SAFE) unless they win a scholarship or join VANGUARD.

items.title: SusHi Tech Challenge 2027 (Tokyo pitch contest)
items.summary: The global startup pitch competition at SusHi Tech Tokyo 2027, Asia's large innovation conference run by the Tokyo government, with a JPY 10 million grand prize. It looks for startups whose technology helps build sustainable, resilient cities.
eligibility: Startups with a new technology or business model and real growth potential
Must already have a product or service in the market
Business should fit the theme of sustainable cities through technology (e.g. physical AI, quantum, resilience, longevity, drug discovery)
Must be able to pitch in person in Tokyo on both event days and staff a booth for all three days (20–22 May 2027)
benefits: JPY 10 million for the grand prize winner
Semifinalists get the JPY 300,000 booth fee waived and a networking session
Planned special awards from corporate partners
Exposure to investors, corporates and the Tokyo government
items.note: Closes 5:00 pm JST on 18 Dec 2026 (1:30 pm IST). Travel to Tokyo is at your own cost; the page mentions no travel support. Read the official application guidelines for any further conditions.

items.title: Social Startups Programme (Cohort 1)
items.amount: ₹45K/month for 8 months, then ₹15–20 lakh/yr seed grant for 2 yrs
items.summary: A new Azim Premji Foundation programme for experienced development professionals who want to found and lead their own grassroots non-profit. About 100 people get a paid eight-month seeding phase to set up the organisation in Odisha, the North-East, Eastern UP or Bengaluru Urban, with a two-year seed grant open to those who hit their milestones.
eligibility: Under 40 years of age
Graduate degree
At least 3 years of ground-level work in the development sector
Must intend to set up and lead a new civil society organisation as a first-time founder
Not already a founder or co-founder of any registered organisation
Willing to relocate to and commit long-term to one of the four focus geographies
benefits: Monthly honorarium of ₹45,000 during the 8-month seeding phase (from 1 April 2027)
One-month residential boot camp and supported fieldwork
Hands-on help with registration, governance, compliance, finance, HR and programme design
Pathway to a two-year grant of ₹15–20 lakh per year for those who meet milestones
items.note: Applications close 31 Dec 2026. This is for founding a non-profit, not a for-profit startup. Selection: screening, document review, statement of purpose, online interview and in-person panel; results expected by Feb 2027. Focus themes include rural livelihoods, health, youth, disability, child welfare, Adivasi well-being and urban informal settlements.

items.title: D-Prize Global Competition 2026–27
items.summary: D-Prize gives first-time social entrepreneurs seed money to launch a venture that delivers an already-proven poverty intervention — such as ORS for childhood diarrhoea, reading glasses, water filters or post-harvest support — to people who still lack it. You pick one of its listed challenges (or propose your own) and pitch a distribution model you can pilot quickly.
eligibility: New ventures only: typically under 18 months of full-time operation and under US$30,000 raised
Existing organisations considered only if their core work is distributing an evidence-based poverty intervention
Must target one of D-Prize's challenge areas or a well-argued 'propose your own' intervention
Founders from low- and middle-income countries such as India are especially encouraged
Willing to run a pilot and then raise follow-on funding to scale
benefits: Up to US$20,000 to launch and pilot the venture
Ongoing guidance from the D-Prize team during the pilot
Credibility with follow-on funders after a successful pilot
Light first round — only a two-page concept note and CVs
items.note: The regular round closed on 15 Nov 2026; the final extension round runs to 6 Dec 2026 at midnight Pacific Time (about 1:30 PM IST on 7 Dec), but you must first register for it on D-Prize's extension page. Round 1 needs a two-page concept note plus founder resumes; the top ~5% get two weeks to answer written questions, then interviews. Only around the top 1% of applicants are funded.

items.title: The Liveability Challenge 2027
items.amount: Up to S$1 million funding per winner
items.summary: A global search for scalable, commercially viable solutions to urban sustainability problems in tropical cities, run across three tracks: Decarbonisation, Cool Earth (resilience and cooling) and Oceans. Top solutions win grant funding and a pitch slot at the Grand Finale in Singapore during Ecosperity Week 2027.
eligibility: Open to startups and ventures worldwide, including India
Solution must address one of the three tracks: Decarbonisation, Cool Earth or Oceans
Must be scalable and commercially viable, with relevance to cities in the tropics
Early-stage to growth-stage companies with a working technology or business model are best placed
benefits: Up to S$1 million in grant funding for top solutions in each track
Decarbonisation finalists can be considered for up to S$2 million in development funding from A*STAR
Oceans finalists can be considered for up to S$500,000 equity investment from the Asia Ocean Fund
Pitch at the Grand Finale in Singapore before investors and corporates
items.note: Submissions close 18 Feb 2027 (check the portal for the exact time, usually Singapore time). The core prize is grant funding, but the A*STAR and Asia Ocean Fund add-ons are separate — the Asia Ocean Fund route is an equity investment. Finalists are expected to attend the Grand Finale in Singapore.

items.title: PRIP Scheme – Second Call (Pharma & MedTech R&D)
items.org: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers
items.amount: Up to ₹5 Cr (early stage) / ₹100 Cr (later stage)
items.summary: The second call of the ₹5,000 crore Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma & MedTech (PRIP) scheme funds startups, MSMEs and industry building new drugs, biosimilars and novel medical devices. Early-stage projects start with a short concept note; later-stage projects apply directly with a detailed proposal.
eligibility: Early-stage track: startups and MSMEs taking a product from TRL 1–3 up to (not beyond) TRL 5
Later-stage track: industry, startups and MSMEs taking a product from TRL 4–6 to higher readiness
Project must fall in a priority area: new chemical/biological entities, phyto-pharmaceuticals, complex generics, biosimilars, or novel medical devices not yet approved by CDSCO
Projects already submitted in PRIP Round 1 should not be resubmitted
Ecosystem enablers (incubators etc.) may submit early-stage concept notes on behalf of startups in their network
benefits: Up to ₹5 crore per early-stage project
Up to ₹100 crore per later-stage project, covering up to 35% of approved project cost
Mentorship for commercialisation, plus MedTech Mitra and Patent Mitra support
Access to a collaboration platform linking industry, academia and startups
items.note: Submission window opened on the PRIP portal from mid-September 2026; no closing date has been announced, so apply early and check the portal. Later-stage awards need the applicant to co-fund at least 65% of the project. Novel device categories include AI/ML devices and SaMD/SiMD, genetic diagnostics, surgical robotics, telemedicine-enabled devices and novel IVDs/biomarkers.

items.title: NLDSL DigiTwin Grand Challenge 2026
items.org: NICDC Logistics Data Services Ltd (NLDSL) with NICDC and DPIIT Startup India
items.amount: ₹3 lakh per sector winner; ₹20–30 lakh+ award pool
items.summary: A government-backed contest to build digital twins of Indian logistics systems — ports, rail and road corridors, warehousing, mining and EV supply chains — using simulated datasets and the ULIP API platform. Stage 1 asks only for team registration and a concept note.
eligibility: Open to students, startups, enterprises, academic and research institutions, and independent innovators based in India
Teams of 2 to 5 members
At least one member must have hands-on skills in data engineering, AI/ML, GIS, modelling/simulation or software development
No participation fee
Teams may enter both the DigiTwin and the Freight Transport Model themes as separate applications
benefits: ₹3 lakh for the best team in each of six DigiTwin tracks (multimodal logistics; industrial corridors, parks and warehousing; mining and minerals; urban mobility and EV logistics; pharma/health/agri supply chains; open category)
Access to simulated logistics datasets and optional official ULIP APIs during prototyping
Virtual demo to a national jury panel in late January 2027
Winners may be enlisted as vendors with NLDSL
items.note: Registration and the 2-page Stage 1 concept note for both themes (DigiTwin and Freight Transport Model) were extended to 30 November 2026 (closing time not stated — submit a day early). Revised indicative timeline: shortlist announced 9 Dec; Stage 2 detailed ideas due 9–18 Dec; prototypes built 29 Dec 2026–18 Jan 2027; jury demos 18–28 Jan; winners announced 29 Jan 2027. The site shows both ₹20 lakh+ and ₹30 lakh+ as the pool, so confirm prize terms in the guidelines, along with IP terms. Help desk: support.digitaltwingc@nldsl.in.

items.title: AI for Good Innovation Factory 2026–27
items.org: ITU (UN International Telecommunication Union) – AI for Good
items.summary: The UN's AI for Good platform runs monthly online pitch rounds from September 2026 to May 2027 for startups using AI against global development challenges. Winners of each round progress towards a Grand Finale at the AI for Good Global Summit in Geneva, where the top startup wins $20,000.
eligibility: Startups worldwide (Indian founders included) with an AI-powered solution
The solution should address one or more UN Sustainable Development Goals
The AI must be central, innovative and able to scale
A working product or pilot strengthens your chances in the live pitch rounds
benefits: $20,000 cash prize for the overall winner
Live online pitch sessions in front of experts, investors and UN agencies
Startup Accelerator Programme in Geneva, 21–24 June 2027, for finalists
Global visibility through the AI for Good Global Summit
items.note: Applications run through ITU's Innovation Factory startup form and feed a series of monthly pitching sessions until May 2027, so apply early to get a slot (one listing names 23 November 2026 for the next intake). The pre-final is on 22 June 2027 and the Grand Finale on 24 June 2027 in Geneva — travel costs aren't stated. ITU warns it is not linked to any paid pitch-coaching services offering 'guaranteed' entry.

items.title: ACHEMA Start-up Award 2027
items.summary: A business-plan competition for young companies and founding teams in chemistry, process engineering and biotechnology, run by the organiser of ACHEMA, the world's largest process-industry trade fair. Up to ten finalists exhibit at ACHEMA 2027 in Frankfurt and the winner receives €15,000.
eligibility: Teams or individuals with a company concept or business plan, or companies founded after 1 January 2024
Venture must be in chemistry, process technology or biotechnology
Product or service must be a market innovation with a clear competitive advantage, explained in the plan
Entries in English or German; at least one named person as founder/contact
No nationality restriction is stated in the terms
benefits: €15,000 prize money for the winner, presented on stage at ACHEMA 2027
Mentors and venture capitalists assigned from the start
Free showcase space for up to ten finalists during ACHEMA, 14–18 June 2027
Jury pitch in February 2027 and exposure to global process-industry buyers
items.note: Full business plans must be submitted by 30 November 2026, along with a signed copy of the terms and conditions. Finalists are picked in January 2027 and must present in person in Frankfurt (February jury pitch and June fair) — budget for travel. File patents before submitting, as plans are shared with jurors and mentors under NDA.

items.title: Nexa Lighthouse — Climate & Health Innovation Call (Asia-Pacific)
items.org: Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation
items.summary: Nexa Lighthouse funds proven, locally led innovations in Asia and the Pacific that help health systems act on climate risks such as extreme heat, air pollution and shifting malaria/dengue patterns. A linked South Asia call focuses on protecting people with diabetes and heart disease from extreme heat.
eligibility: Incorporated organisations based in Asia-Pacific (India included): companies, social enterprises, NGOs, non-profits, research institutions or government bodies
Individuals, sole proprietorships, unincorporated trusts and partnerships cannot apply
Innovation must already be proven and ready to scale — this is not early-idea money
Solution must be locally led and address a climate-linked health threat (heat, air quality, vector-borne disease)
benefits: Transition to Scale investment of roughly $250,000 to $2 million per innovation, sized by maturity
Backing from Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN's network of Asian funders
Support to embed the solution with local health actors and systems
items.note: Proposals are due 17 November 2026 at 2:00 pm ET (12:30 am IST on 18 November) via Grand Challenges Canada's Fluxx portal — apply through that portal, not the Novo Nordisk Foundation, or you risk disqualification. Funding instrument (grant vs. repayable/equity-linked) is set at the partners' discretion. The South Asia cardiometabolic-heat strand must be framed around heat protection for patients, not general climate adaptation.

items.title: UpLink AI for Plastic Value Chain Transformation Challenge
items.org: UpLink (World Economic Forum) with the WEF Circular Economy Transformation Initiative
items.amount: Non-cash: UpLink Ventures recognition, WEF access & visibility
items.summary: The World Economic Forum's open-innovation platform is looking for early-stage ventures that use AI to fix the plastics value chain, from designing better materials and products to sorting, recovering and returning hard-to-recycle waste to industry. Selected teams join a 2027 UpLink cohort with access to WEF's plastics and circular-economy community.
eligibility: Early-stage ventures with an AI-driven solution for some part of the plastics value chain; open globally, Indian startups included

Must choose one primary track: better material/product design, making recovered or alternative materials work in production, high-purity data-rich recovery, or turning hard-to-recycle waste into usable feedstock
Ventures already named UpLink Ventures in an earlier challenge are not eligible
Judged on solution quality, impact, scalability of the business model, traction signals and team
benefits: Recognition as an UpLink Venture of the World Economic Forum
Access to selected WEF and partner events, projects and communities, including the Plastics Technology and Innovation workstream
Visibility through WEF and UpLink channels — useful for corporate pilots and investor credibility
Chance to contribute a case study to WEF's Plastics and Technology report (planned for summer 2027)
items.note: Submissions close 2 December 2026 at 11:59 pm CET (about 4:29 am IST on 3 December). There is no cash prize — the value is WEF network access and visibility. Timeline: review Dec 2026–Feb 2027, pitch day March 2027, cohort announced April 2027, programme starts May 2027. No application fee is mentioned.

items.title: Bihar Startup Policy — Interest-Free Seed Fund up to ₹10 Lakh
items.org: Department of Industries, Government of Bihar (Startup Bihar)
items.summary: Under the Bihar Startup Policy 2022–27, startups recognised by the state can get a seed loan of up to ₹10 lakh at zero interest, repayable over ten years and released in milestone-linked tranches. Women, SC/ST and differently-abled founders get an added top-up on the standard limits.
eligibility: Startup must be registered and recognised by the Startup Bihar nodal agency (Department of Industries) via the Startup Bihar portal
Business operating from Bihar with an innovative, scalable product or service
Funding size is decided after a rating-agency assessment and review by the State Startup Monitoring and Implementation Committee (SMIC)
Extra incentives (5% women, 5% SC/ST, 15% differently-abled) apply only where the startup is wholly owned by founders from that category
benefits: Seed support of up to ₹10 lakh as a 10-year interest-free loan, released in tranches against milestones
Usable for idea validation, prototyping, market research, travel, training, marketing and initial setup
Matching loan up to the amount raised from angel groups or Category-I AIFs
Incubation cost reimbursement (up to ₹2 lakh, paid to incubator), patent filing support, free valuation at commercialisation, and procurement preference
items.note: Rolling — apply through the Startup Bihar portal (startup.bihar.gov.in) after getting state recognition; helpline 1800 345 6214, startup-bihar@gov.in. This is a loan, not a grant: it must be repaid over 10 years. The actual amount depends on the rating-agency score, and the current policy runs until 2027.

items.title: Haryana Seed Funding for Startups Scheme — up to ₹10 Lakh
items.org: Department of Industries & Commerce, Government of Haryana (Startup Haryana)
items.summary: Haryana gives DPIIT-recognised startups with a registered office in the state a non-repayable seed grant of up to ₹10 lakh, paid in three tranches. Applications are reviewed quarterly by an evaluation committee and the scheme accepts entries until the policy ends in July 2027.
eligibility: Registered with Startup Haryana as a Category 1 startup (requires DPIIT recognition and a registered office in Haryana)
Must hold a Haryana Udyam Memorandum (HUM)
Product or service must not be on the state's restricted list; otherwise sector-agnostic
Cannot claim a similar incentive for the same purpose under another state policy
Must score at least 60/100 in the Evaluation & Approval Committee assessment (a presentation may be required)
benefits: Non-repayable seed grant of up to ₹10 lakh per startup
Released 50% / 40% / 10%, each later tranche after a utilisation certificate
Travel and field/market-research costs covered up to ₹50,000 each within the grant
Rejected applicants can reapply in a later quarter
items.note: Effectively rolling: applications are taken any time and considered in the quarter after submission, but must be in before the policy expires on 6 July 2027. Apply online on the Industries & Commerce Department portal. Documents: authorisation letter, representative's PAN and photo, notarised undertaking, HUM copy, cancelled cheque and pitch deck; deficiencies must be fixed within 10 working days. Tranche claims need CA-certified utilisation certificates and invoices. Quotas are capped by block category (A–D).

items.title: Startup Odisha — Monthly Allowance & Product Development/Marketing Assistance
items.org: Startup Odisha, MSME Department, Government of Odisha
items.amount: ₹20K–22K/month allowance; up to ₹15–16 lakh product/marketing assistance
items.summary: Startups recognised by Startup Odisha can draw a monthly sustenance allowance at the idea/prototype stage and, once commercialised, a one-time grant for product development and marketing/publicity. Women, transgender and SC/ST/SEBC/PH founders get higher limits.
eligibility: Startup must be recognised by Startup Odisha (state recognition is the first step for all schemes)
Monthly allowance is for idea/prototype-stage startups
Product development & marketing assistance is for startups that have commercialised their idea
Higher amounts apply if a founder/co-founder is a woman, transgender person, or from SC/ST/SEBC/PH categories (women-led needs at least 50% women equity)
benefits: Monthly allowance of ₹20,000 (₹22,000 for women/transgender/SC/ST/SEBC/PH founders) — women-led startups get it for one year
Product development and marketing/publicity assistance of up to ₹15 lakh (₹16 lakh for the categories above)
Both are non-repayable and equity-free
Access to O-Hub and the wider Startup Odisha ecosystem
items.note: Rolling — no fixed closing date; apply through the Startup Odisha portal after recognition. Assistance is typically released on a reimbursement/milestone basis, so keep bills and progress records. Confirm current terms with Startup Odisha (O-Hub, Bhubaneswar; toll-free 1800-345-7100) before planning around the full amount.

items.title: Antler India — AI Residency & Direct Pre-Seed Investment
items.summary: Antler India backs very early founders, either through a quarterly Bengaluru residency focused on AI-first startups or by investing directly in pre-launch teams. Its standard deal is up to about ₹4 crore for 11% equity, with decisions in a few weeks.
eligibility: Pre-launch, pre-product or pre-revenue teams; AI-first ideas are the focus but other exceptional ideas are considered
Founders must be full-time and actively testing with users
Residency participants must be able to relocate to Bengaluru for the in-person portion
Solo founders and teams can apply; a warm referral helps but is not required
benefits: Pre-seed investment of up to about ₹4 crore for 11% equity, with potential follow-on capital
Residency: 2-week in-person programme in Bengaluru with partner office hours and 1-on-1s with AI builders
One-time ₹2 lakh grant to residency founders for expenses, plus office space in Bengaluru
AI and cloud perks worth over $1M (up to $4M in total perks)
items.note: Rolling — apply any time via antler.co/apply; residencies run roughly every quarter on a ~45-day cycle (dates are announced on Antler's cohort page). This is equity money (11%), not a grant, and Antler invests in only part of each residency cohort. Founders not yet ready can join the free Before Day Zero community.

items.title: Entrepreneur First — Bangalore Winter 2027 Programme
items.amount: Up to $250K (~₹2.2 crore) pre-seed for selected companies
items.summary: EF's Bangalore programme recruits individual technical and entrepreneurial people before they have a co-founder or an idea, helps them form a team and a company over 14 weeks in Bangalore, then moves funded teams to San Francisco. The Winter 2027 cohort starts in February 2027 and 1 December 2026 is the cut-off for its third selection round.
eligibility: Individuals apply, not companies: you do not need a co-founder or a startup idea
Aimed at early-career people with exceptional results relative to their peers, typically technical or commercial builders
Must be able to commit full-time and in person in Bangalore for the 14-week programme
Funded companies are expected to relocate and build from San Francisco after the Bangalore phase (EF may help with visas but does not provide them)
Existing co-founders can apply, but each person should submit their own application and mention the other
benefits: Structured co-founder matching and idea development alongside a cohort of other founders
Pre-seed investment for companies EF backs: reported terms are $125K on a post-money SAFE for 8%, plus an optional further $125K on an uncapped MFN SAFE
A further 3 months in San Francisco after the Bangalore phase for funded teams
Access to EF's global investor and alumni network
items.note: Apply by 1 December 2026 to be considered in the third of four selection rounds for Winter 2027 (programme starts February 2027). This is equity investment, not a grant, and only teams EF chooses to back receive money. Investment terms come from EF's published standard deal as reported by third parties; confirm the India terms at interview. Expect to relocate to San Francisco if funded.

items.title: Google for Startups Cloud Program — AI Tier (up to $350K credits)
items.amount: Up to $350K (~₹3 crore) in Google Cloud credits over 2 years
items.summary: Google Cloud gives venture-backed startups free cloud credits for two years, with AI-first companies building on Gemini eligible for up to $350,000. It is in-kind support for compute, storage and Google's AI models rather than cash, and applications are open year-round.
eligibility: Founded within the last five years

Raised a pre-seed or seed round from institutional investors/VCs in the last five years, or a Series A in the last 12 months (SAFEs count; angel, grant, prize and friends-and-family money do not qualify for this tier)
Has not already received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits
Uses or plans to use Gemini as a foundation of the main product to get the AI-first amount
Not a consultancy, agency, dev shop, non-profit, educational or government body, or crypto-mining company; company domain must not have had a paid Google Workspace plan in the 31 days before applying
benefits: AI-first startups: 100% of usage covered up to $250K in year 1, plus 20% up to another $100K in year 2
Other eligible startups: up to $100K in year 1 plus up to $100K in year 2 (up to $200K total)
Credits usable on Google Cloud services and Google's own models (Gemini, Gemma)
Webinars and Q&As with Google Cloud AI product teams, and access to the Gemini Startup Forum
items.note: Rolling. Credits are in-kind (not cash) and third-party models on Google Cloud are billed separately. Bootstrapped or angel-funded startups do not qualify for this tier but may be considered for Google's lower Start tier. Approval is at Google's discretion; keep your funding documents and company website ready.

items.title: AWS Activate — Cloud Credits for Startups (up to $200K)
items.amount: $1K–$5K (bootstrapped) or up to $200K (investor-backed) in AWS credits
items.summary: AWS Activate gives startups free AWS cloud credits: bootstrapped founders can apply directly for up to $5,000, while startups backed by an approved accelerator, angel network or VC can receive up to $200,000. Applications are open all year and decisions usually take one to two weeks.
eligibility: Pre-Series B startup founded in the last 10 years
AWS account on a paid-tier plan
New to Activate credits, or requesting more than previously received
For the Portfolio tier (up to $200K): backed by an AWS Activate Provider (accelerator, incubator, angel or VC) and able to supply that provider's Org ID
benefits: Activate Founders: credits starting at $1,000, up to $5,000, for self-funded startups
Activate Portfolio: up to $200,000 in credits through an Activate Provider
Access to 200+ AWS services including AI and data tools, plus Kiro startup credits for eligible startups
Invite-only AI credits beyond $200K for scaling AI startups, and migration support credits
items.note: Rolling; apply with an AWS Builder ID using your work email, choose your tier, add company and funding details, then link an AWS account. Replies typically arrive in 5–10 business days. Credits are in-kind and carry expiry dates under AWS's promotional credit terms. Ask your incubator whether it is an Activate Provider — many Indian incubators are, which unlocks the bigger tier.

items.title: World Economic Forum Technology Pioneers 2027
items.amount: No cash — free 2-year WEF community membership
items.summary: The Forum picks around 100 early-stage frontier-tech companies worldwide each year for a two-year membership that brings them into WEF meetings, initiatives and publications; the 2027 call is open to Indian startups at no cost.
eligibility: Company commercialising frontier or cutting-edge technology with a workable business model
At Series A funding stage
Less than 10 years since incorporation
Independent and privately held
Demonstrable positive impact on society or the planet, and leadership willing to give time to Forum activities
benefits: Two-year membership of the Technology Pioneers community, with no fee
Invitations to Forum meetings and multi-stakeholder initiatives alongside governments and large corporates
Platform to publish thought leadership through Forum Stories
Access to WEF research and the strategic intelligence platform
Global visibility when the cohort is announced in June 2027
items.note: Applications close 31 Jan 2027 at midnight Pacific Time (about 1:30 pm IST on 1 Feb). No fee at any stage. Review runs Feb–Apr 2027 and the cohort is announced in June 2027. This is recognition and network access, not funding — travel to events is usually at your own cost.

items.title: Allianz x Social Shifters MoveNow Social Innovation Challenge 2026
items.summary: A worldwide challenge for founders aged 18–30 tackling social or environmental problems in underserved communities; three themes each award one US$10,000 grant and four US$5,000 grants, plus an Allianz business mentor for finalists.
eligibility: Founders aged 18–30, based anywhere in the world (Indians eligible)
Youth-led startup, venture or project addressing a clearly defined social or environmental problem
Solution designed for and with underserved communities
Must fit one theme: financial confidence in the digital economy, closing the health gap, or community-led climate resilience
benefits: Grants of US$10,000 (one per theme) or US$5,000 (four per theme), equity-free
Mentoring from an Allianz business expert for finalists
Exposure through the Social Shifters global network
items.note: Deadline 18 Dec 2026 (no closing time published — submit by 17 Dec IST to be safe). Age is checked strictly; the lead applicant must be 18–30. Theme 1 targets tools that help entrepreneurs and SMEs manage money online; theme 2 focuses on women and marginalised groups in health; theme 3 on vulnerable rural and urban climate adaptation.

items.title: António Champalimaud Vision Award 2027
items.summary: One of the world's largest prizes in vision, the 2027 edition rewards organisations fighting blindness and visual impairment, mainly in developing regions, or building technology that improves life for blind and visually impaired people — a strong fit for Indian eye-care NGOs, hospitals and assistive-tech ventures.
eligibility: Organisations of any size — local, national, regional or international — can apply or be nominated
Work must reduce blindness or visual impairment, primarily in developing countries, and/or deliver innovations that improve quality of life for visually impaired people
Collaborative, multi-institution or multidisciplinary efforts are welcome
A proven track record of productive work is expected (this is an award for results, not a seed grant)
benefits: €1,000,000 prize, usable for any non-commercial purpose that advances the laureates' work
International recognition at the award ceremony in Lisbon
Entries stay active for three award cycles, with updates allowed
items.note: Applications and nominations close 31 Dec 2026; supplementary material can be sent in the first half of January 2027 if you notify the Foundation (award@fchampalimaud.org). Prize money cannot be used for commercial purposes, so early-stage for-profit startups are a weak fit. Odd-year awards focus on public-health and assistive work; even years go to research.

items.title: Lee Kuan Yew Global Business Plan Competition 2027 (13th edition)
items.org: Institute of Innovation & Entrepreneurship, Singapore Management University (SMU)
items.amount: Share of a S$2.5M+ prize pool (cash, grants, investment, in-kind)
items.summary: SMU's flagship global competition is looking for university-linked founders building deep-tech answers to urban and sustainability problems, from climate and energy to mobility, food systems and longevity. Fifty finalists are flown to Singapore for the finals, and the strongest can move into SMU's Urban SustaInnovator accelerator and fund.
eligibility: At least one founder must be currently enrolled at a university or have graduated within the last five years
Startup must address one of the competition's 12 urban/sustainability focus areas (e.g. climate tech, energy, food and land use, urban mobility, longevity/healthtech, sustainable materials)
Two tracks: 'Beta' for 0-to-1 ventures and 'Infinity' for 1-to-scale ventures
Open to founders from any country, including India
Registration is free via the competition's Agorize page
benefits: Share of a total prize pool above S$2.5 million, mixing cash, grants, investment opportunities and in-kind support
Finalists flown to Singapore for the finals and Innovation Festival (28 Sep – 1 Oct 2027)
Investor, mentor and corporate introductions during finals week
Selected finalists can join SMU's Urban SustaInnovator (USI) accelerator and be considered by its fund
items.note: Final registration closes 31 Mar 2027; an early-bird round closes 31 Jan 2027, so registering early is wise. No closing time zone is published — treat it as Singapore time (IST+2:30). The university link is a hard requirement: a founder without a current enrolment or a degree from the last five years makes the team ineligible.

items.title: AI for Livelihoods Hackathon 2026 (Women's Economic Empowerment)
items.org: IIMA Ventures (IIM Ahmedabad) with SEWA Bharat, PRADAN and Hand in Hand India, supported by the Gates Foundation
items.amount: ₹5 lakh pilot grant; follow-on up to ₹50 lakh
items.summary: IIMA Ventures is looking for AI-led products that measurably raise the incomes of low-income women in India, with problem statements set by three large grassroots organisations. Winners get money and a real field partner to pilot with, which is often harder to find than the cash.
eligibility: Teams building a technology (AI-enabled) solution that increases earnings or economic agency for low-income women in India
Idea, product and revenue-stage teams can apply — you do not need a registered company to submit
Must incorporate as an Indian entity before your selection is confirmed
Solution should fit one of the challenge problems posed by SEWA Bharat, PRADAN or Hand in Hand India
Teams that have been through other incubators or programmes are not excluded
benefits: ₹5 lakh grant to pilot the solution with the challenge partner's community network
Shortlisted solutions can be considered for follow-on funding of up to ₹50 lakh to scale
Field access to SEWA Bharat, PRADAN or Hand in Hand India users for testing
Mentoring and investor exposure through IIMA Ventures' women's economic empowerment programme
No relocation required
items.note: Applications close 19 November 2026 via the Typeform linked on the IIMA Ventures page (exact closing time not published — submit by the evening of the 18th to be safe). The hackathon grant is presented as equity-free, but startups that are later onboarded as full IIMA Ventures incubatees are normally asked for 2–5% mentoring equity — clarify before signing anything. Have a short pitch deck, a description of the women-income problem you solve and any pilot data ready.

items.title: SPARKS 2.0 Grant for Deep-Tech Startups
items.org: PI-RAHI (PU–IIT Ropar Regional Accelerator for Holistic Innovations), Northern Region S&T Cluster under the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser
items.summary: SPARKS 2.0 gives research-driven startups with a working MVP (TRL 4+) a grant of up to ₹10 lakh plus mentoring, IP and commercialisation help from the PU–IIT Ropar science-and-technology cluster. It is pitched at north Indian founders but is not restricted to them.
eligibility: Startup or innovator with a product or service at MVP stage, technology at TRL 4 or higher
Registered as a Private Limited Company, or willing to incorporate as one within three months of selection

Innovation must fit at least one theme: agriculture & food processing; sustainable mobility & green energy; pharma, medical devices & healthcare; waste management & waste-to-wealth; indigenous technology development; or a cross-theme idea
Preference for entities registered in Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh or Jammu & Kashmir, or targeting markets there — others may still apply
benefits: Grant support of up to ₹10 lakh, subject to selection and programme terms
Expert mentorship from the Panjab University–IIT Ropar ecosystem
Help with IP protection and commercialisation strategy
Introductions to investors and further funding sources
Acceleration support after selection
items.note: Last date 23 November 2026; apply through the Google Form linked on the PI-RAHI SPARKS 2.0 page. Process: online application → screening → shortlisted teams pitch to an evaluation panel. PI-RAHI has not published equity terms or a required-documents list, so email coo@pi-rahi.com if that matters to you. Keep TRL evidence, incorporation details (or a plan to incorporate within 3 months) and a short technical deck handy.

items.title: Cities Deliver: AI Solutions for Public Services
items.org: The Rockefeller Foundation with the OpenAI Foundation
items.summary: A $50 million global grant programme for teams that partner with a city to deploy AI that improves public services for underserved residents — in health, economic mobility, environmental resilience or civic services. Indian non-profits, public benefit companies and, in limited cases, for-profit startups can apply if they have a city government on board.
eligibility: Lead applicant must be a non-profit (including university labs and fiscally sponsored groups), a public benefit corporation, or a for-profit company whose project is charitable and benefits the business only incidentally
Must have a city partner — a city of 50,000+ residents with its own municipal government — that provides a letter of intent; governments cannot apply directly

Project must use AI to improve access to or quality of public services for poor, vulnerable or underserved communities in public health, economic mobility, environmental resilience or civic engagement (election/voting projects excluded)
Open globally including India; organisations in countries under comprehensive US OFAC sanctions are excluded
For-profits must disclose their business model, show an open-source approach for lasting public benefit, and ring-fence grant funds
benefits: Seed track: $500,000 to under $1 million for early concepts ready for a first city pilot
Scale track: $1–2 million for solutions already piloted in a city with early results
24-month grant, half paid upfront and half after a mid-term milestone
No equity taken
Visibility within a global cohort backed by the Rockefeller and OpenAI foundations
items.note: Round 1 closes 29 November 2026 at 11:59 pm US Eastern (about 10:29 am IST on 30 November) on the citiesdeliver.rockefellerfoundation.org portal. Round 1 needs an eligibility screen, a short video demo of the AI solution, a certificate of incorporation (or 501(c)(3)-equivalency/fiscal-sponsor proof) and a city partner's letter of intent — getting the city letter is the real bottleneck, so start now. Shortlisted teams interview in January 2027 and submit full proposals by 1 March 2027. For-profit applicants cannot claim indirect costs.

items.title: Start-Up Chile BIG 13 (Build, Ignite & Growth)
items.amount: Up to CLP 75 million (~₹69 lakh), equity-free
items.summary: Chile's government-backed accelerator is taking applications for its 13th generation, with three tracks: Build (4 months, for teams moving from validated idea to first prototype), Ignite (4 months, for startups with an MVP chasing product-market fit) and Growth (6 months, for companies scaling and raising capital). Founders from any country can apply, and selected foreign teams get help with a work visa and setting up in Chile.
eligibility: Technology-based, innovative and scalable startups from any country and any industry
Build: idea validated, working towards an initial prototype
Ignite: functional product (MVP) with early validation and under about three years of development
Growth: companies already expanding and looking to raise capital
Applicants must clear an eligibility check against the BIG 13 terms and conditions before evaluation
benefits: Equity-free funding: about CLP 15 million (Build, co-financed), CLP 30 million (Ignite) or CLP 75 million (Growth)
Free co-working space in Chile and discounts on partner services
Board sessions, training and access to Start-Up Chile's corporate and investor networks
Support to obtain a work visa and set up operations in Chile
Higher funding share (up to 90%) for teams with women leaders under the Female Founder Factor
items.note: Applications close 24 Nov 2026 at 1:00 PM Chile time (GMT-3), which is 9:30 PM IST. Programmes start in the first half of 2027. Funding is in Chilean pesos and Build requires co-financing from the startup. Expect to run your business from Chile during the programme — read the BIG 13 terms on the site before applying.

items.title: NVIDIA Inception Program for AI Startups
items.amount: Free membership: cloud credits, hardware discounts, training and investor intros
items.summary: NVIDIA's free, always-open programme for startups building with AI, accelerated computing or data science. Members get preferred pricing on NVIDIA hardware and software, partner cloud credits, free technical training and a route to NVIDIA's network of venture investors — with no cohorts, fees or equity.
eligibility: Company is officially incorporated (you must give the incorporation date)
Less than 10 years old
Has at least one developer on the team
Has a working company website
Not a consultancy or outsourced dev shop, crypto-related company, cloud provider, reseller/distributor or listed public company
benefits: Preferred pricing on selected NVIDIA hardware and software
Free cloud credits and offers from NVIDIA and its partners
Free self-paced NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute courses and discounted instructor-led workshops
Possible introductions to venture investors through Inception Capital Connect
Member badge, co-marketing opportunities and access to NVIDIA events
items.note: Rolling — apply any time through the Inception portal; there are no deadlines or cohorts. A pitch deck is required with the application, and revenue or funding is not required. Benefits are mainly in-kind (no cash grant); keep your company profile updated in the portal to stay eligible.

items.title: India Pitch-Pilot-Scale Startup Challenge (AMRUT 2.0) – Reopened
items.org: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) with MyGov
items.amount: Up to ₹20 lakh grant per startup
items.summary: MoHUA has reopened its AMRUT 2.0 startup challenge, which pays DPIIT-recognised startups up to ₹20 lakh to pilot their technology with an Indian city body and then scale it. Problem areas span urban water supply, sewage and used-water reuse, flooding, air quality, street lighting, municipal energy use and heat resilience.
eligibility: Must be a DPIIT-recognised startup

Solution must fit one of the 12 listed themes, e.g. fresh-water systems, hydro-informatics, non-revenue water, sewerage, used-water management, urban flooding, water governance, air quality, municipal energy efficiency, smart street lighting or urban heat resilience
Should be able to run a field pilot with an urban local body (ULB) and show measurable results
Applications are submitted online through the MyGov Innovate India portal
benefits: Grant of up to ₹20 lakh, released in three milestone-linked tranches of ₹5 lakh, ₹7 lakh and ₹8 lakh
Pilot deployment with a city/ULB, which serves as a government reference customer
Mentoring, plus MoHUA support to scale through industry and ULB partnerships
Ministry citation and national visibility for successful startups
items.note: Submission window reopened 10 Nov 2026 and closes 15 Dec 2026; the portal does not state a closing hour, so submit by the evening of 14 Dec to be safe. Keep your DPIIT certificate, a short pitch describing the problem statement you are solving and a pilot plan with measurable outcomes ready. The catch: the money is not upfront — tranches are released only as pilot milestones are met with the partner city.

items.title: Entrepreneurship World Cup 2027 (Riyadh Global Finals)
items.org: Global Entrepreneurship Network (GEN) with Saudi partners
items.amount: US$1 million cash prize pool (top prize US$200,000)
items.summary: One of the world's largest free pitch competitions, open to founders in 160+ countries including India, with separate tracks for idea, early and growth-stage ventures plus four AI sub-tracks. The top 100 are flown to Riyadh for the Global Finals in November 2027 to compete for US$1 million in cash.
eligibility: Individuals or legally registered entities in good standing in their home country (not in liquidation or bankruptcy)
Founder or authorised representative must be 18 or older
Idea track: validated concept, no revenue needed; Early track: registered entity with a working product or prototype and under US$1M annual revenue
Growth track: over US$1M annual revenue or significant traction such as a Series A round
AI sub-tracks are open to companies at any stage; applicants must not be under international sanctions
benefits: Cash prizes: Early Stage US$200k/150k/90k/50k, Growth Stage US$160k/100k, Idea Stage US$30k/20k, and US$50k for each of four AI sub-tracks
All-expenses-paid trip to Riyadh for the Global Finals
Mentoring and a virtual bootcamp for all top-100 finalists, plus investor introductions
Optional Saudi soft-landing support, pilot access with large projects and residency pathways
items.note: Registration has been extended to 31 May 2027; there is no entry fee. After registration come venture refinement, global selection and a virtual bootcamp before the top 100 are named. Finalists must attend in person in Riyadh (Nov 2027), must submit supporting documents within five business days when asked, and pay their own local taxes and bank charges on prize money. Organisers may move you to a different track if your traction does not match the one you picked.

items.title: Aarohan 7.0 — TIH IIT Bombay Seed Support Programme
items.org: TIH Foundation for IoT & IoE, IIT Bombay (under DST's NM-ICPS mission)
items.summary: IIT Bombay's IoT Technology Innovation Hub is investing up to ₹1 crore in startups whose IoT or AI-powered autonomous products are already proven in the field (TRL 6+). This edition targets four areas: autonomous systems for factories, warehouses and logistics; field and inspection systems for farms and infrastructure; assistive and autonomous systems for hospitals; and tech for dairy, livestock and animal husbandry.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup, or able to give an undertaking that it qualifies for DPIIT recognition
Indian promoters must hold at least 51% of shares on the date of application
Technology must be core to the product or business model and sit within the IoT domain
Product at Technology Readiness Level 6 or higher, i.e. demonstrated in a real environment and moving to deployment or sales — idea-stage teams are not eligible
Must not have taken investment from any other NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub (earlier grants from a TIH are fine)
benefits: Up to ₹1 crore invested as equity or CCPS, released in tranches against milestones you propose
Business and technical mentoring from TIH IIT Bombay
Access to the hub's labs, facilities and technical resources as per hub policy
Visibility through TIH events and connections across the national NM-ICPS hub network
items.note: Apply online by 22 November 2026 (no closing time is published, so don't leave it to the last evening). Keep ready: certificate of incorporation, MoA/AoA, company PAN, DPIIT certificate or eligibility undertaking, up to three years of financial statements, a fully diluted cap table on letterhead, and the budget/milestone sheet and pitch deck in TIH's own templates (downloadable from the programme page). This is an investment, not a grant — expect equity or CCPS terms and an investment committee review after a possible pitch round. Queries: entredevelopment@tihiitb.org.

items.title: Imagine H2O Accelerator & Imagine H2O Asia — 2027 Cohorts
items.org: Imagine H2O (global non-profit water innovation accelerator)
items.amount: Mentoring, investor access + pilot co-funding (up to US$125K in recent cohorts)
items.summary: Imagine H2O has opened applications for its 2027 global Water Accelerator and its Asia programme, aimed at early-stage water technology companies that have finished a proof of concept. Selected startups get mentors, introductions to water-focused investors and utilities, and a route to funded pilot projects; the cohort is announced in April 2027.
eligibility: For-profit startup that is less than 10 years old
Annual revenue below US$5 million
Proof of concept already completed
Equity raised below US$10 million for the global Accelerator, or below US$20 million for Imagine H2O Asia
Solution must address water — e.g. utilities, industrial water, agriculture water use, water quality or resilience
benefits: Year-long mentoring from water-industry experts, investors and founders
Introductions to water-focused venture capital and potential customers such as utilities and industrial users
Pilot support: recent cohorts could access co-funding of up to US$25K (Asia, with ADB and Singapore partners) and up to US$125K from Imagine H2O's Water Innovation Pilot Fund
Global visibility through Imagine H2O's network and events; the Asia track adds in-country advisors and customer meetings across South and Southeast Asia
items.note: Applications close Friday 20 November 2026 (US time — submit by 19 November in India to be safe). The 2027 cohort is announced in April 2027. Pilot-fund amounts above are from the 2026 programme and are competitive, not guaranteed. The organiser has not published fee or equity terms in its announcement; read the terms on the application page before applying.

items.title: RE:FRAME PropTech Accelerator — Cohort 01
items.amount: Pitch for a ₹15 Cr investment pool + 7 coworking seats
items.summary: A four-week accelerator for Indian PropTech startups run by media house Inc42 and listed workspace operator DevX: three weeks online, then a residential bootcamp and Demo Day in Delhi NCR in March 2027. Only 10 startups get in, and the shortlisted few pitch for a shared ₹15 crore investment pool.
eligibility: Startup registered and headquartered in India, incorporated on or after 1 January 2020
Working product with early customers — annual revenue roughly ₹1 Cr to ₹8 Cr
Bootstrapped, seed or pre-Series A funding stage
Solution anywhere in the real-estate value chain (construction, leasing, property management, financing, facilities, etc.)
Founders able to attend every virtual session and the full Delhi NCR bootcamp
Startups missing one criterion may still apply and are judged on traction, problem, market, team and scalability
benefits: Mentor-led curriculum on enterprise sales and GTM, unit economics, product/AI and fundraising readiness
Demo Day pitch to investors for a share of a ₹15 Cr investment pool (subject to due diligence and agreed terms)
7 DevX coworking seats for each shortlisted startup, with additional seats at 10% off
Introductions to enterprise buyers in real estate, plus visibility across Inc42 and DevX channels
No programme fee and no equity taken just for participating
items.note: Applications close 20 December 2026; selections in January 2027, online phase in February and the Delhi NCR bootcamp plus Demo Day in March 2027. Founders pay their own travel and stay for the bootcamp. Any investment from the pool is a separate deal on mutually agreed terms (so it may involve equity) and you can decline it without losing your place.

items.title: GSMA Innovation Fund for AI-Enabled Financial Health
items.summary: GSMA's new grant round backs for-profit companies in low- and middle-income countries that use AI and mobile technology to improve the financial health of underserved people — for example credit, savings, insurance or money-management tools. Grants of £100K–£250K fund a 15–18 month project to scale a solution that already has users and revenue.
eligibility: For-profit private company with up to 250 employees (governments, NGOs, universities, mobile operators, incubators and UN agencies cannot be lead applicants)
Registered and operating in the ODA-eligible country where the project will run — the project can cover one or at most two countries (India is on the OECD DAC list)
Already has active users and commercial revenue in an eligible country, with most income from commercial activity
Solution uses digital — especially mobile — technology and AI to serve low-income or underserved users
Must bring matching funds of at least 25% of the grant requested
Not eligible: research-only work, new hardware development, or already-proven solutions with nothing innovative
benefits: Non-dilutive grant of £100,000–£250,000 over 15–18 months
Up to 10% of the grant can cover eligible direct overheads
Technical assistance and visibility through GSMA's Mobile for Development network
Connections to mobile operators and the wider GSMA ecosystem for scaling
items.note: Stage 1 (eligibility check and application form, in English) closes 17 December 2026 at 23:59 UTC — that is 5:29 AM IST on 18 December, so submit on the 17th. Before contracting you need at least one year of audited financial statements, evidence of the 25% match, sound financial systems and a bank account that can receive GBP. The grant pays costs only (no profit margin). Confirm your country on the FAQ page's eligible list before applying.

items.title: T Challenge 2027 — Shaping a World of Connected Intelligence
items.summary: Deutsche Telekom and T-Mobile US are looking for ideas that make future networks smarter, greener and more trustworthy — from autonomous self-running networks to 6G products, sensing and quantum tech. Shortlisted teams build their concept with a Telekom mentor and pitch for prize money in Bonn.
eligibility: Open worldwide to startups, developers, researchers, university teams and companies — Indian applicants can apply
Applicants must be 18 or older (or have guardian consent)
Current Deutsche Telekom / T-Mobile employees and government bodies cannot enter; team leads must not have worked for the group in the past 36 months
Idea must fit one of the 2027 themes: trusted autonomous networks, energy-adaptable infrastructure, 6G products and experiences, sensing and physical intelligence, or quantum technologies
Teams should be able to turn the idea into at least a working MVP during the build phase
benefits: Cash prizes for the top three teams plus a possible special award, paid without taking equity
One-to-one mentoring from a Telekom expert during the build phase (Feb–May 2027)
Finalist teams flown to the final pitch and awards in Bonn in May 2027, with travel and hotel covered by Telekom
Direct exposure to Telekom and T-Mobile executives and possible pilots or partnerships
items.note: Idea submissions close 9 Jan 2027 (reported cut-off 23:59 CET, i.e. about 4:29 AM IST on 10 Jan). The first round is a written idea submission; finalists then build an MVP and pitch in Bonn on 11–12 May 2027. Visa costs are not covered. Prize amounts above come from the published rules — re-check the official portal before relying on them.

items.title: South Summit Madrid 2027 — Startup Competition
items.amount: No cash prize; free stage pitch, investor matchmaking and tickets
items.summary: One of Europe's biggest startup competitions picks 100 finalists from around the world to pitch on the main stage in Madrid in front of investors and corporates. It is free to enter and a strong route into European investor and customer networks.
eligibility: Startups from any country, sector and stage — Indian startups are eligible
The startup must be legally incorporated in its home country
Must fit one of ten verticals, from Applied AI and AI agents to energy and climate, health, fintech, cybersecurity, defence/space and education
Finalists must pitch in person, in English, in Madrid (2–4 June 2027)
Past applicants may reapply and are judged on progress since their last entry
benefits: 3-minute pitch on the main stage, with a chance at one of five competition awards
Two free event passes for the team and one-to-one investor and corporate matchmaking
Listing in the event's Investor Book and Corporate Book, plus a training programme in May
Discounted demo booth; even non-finalists who complete 100% of the profile receive a free entry ticket
items.note: Applications close 31 Jan 2027; you can save a draft and edit until then. Around 400 startups are pre-selected in February and the 100 finalists are told in the second week of April. Entry and participation are free, but travel and accommodation to Madrid are at your own cost.

items.title: South Summit Brazil 2027 — Startup Competition (Porto Alegre)
items.amount: No cash prize; stage pitch, mentoring and investor access
items.summary: South Summit's Latin American edition selects 50 startups from anywhere in the world to pitch to international investors, corporates and media in Porto Alegre in April 2027. A useful, free entry point for Indian startups eyeing Brazil and the wider LatAm market.
eligibility: Startups from any country — Indian startups can apply
Any sector and any stage of development
Finalists must be able to travel to Porto Alegre, Brazil, for the event on 14–16 April 2027
Selection is by an expert committee that includes potential investors
benefits: 3-minute stage pitch in front of international investors, corporates and press
Competition awards for Best Team, Most Scalable, Most Disruptive, Most Sustainable and Global Winner
Mentoring and training sessions in March 2027 and networking with other finalists and investors
50% off event tickets and special rates for a marketplace exhibition stand
items.note: Registration is free and closes 14 Dec 2026. The jury picks 50 finalists in January and announces them in February 2027. There is no cash prize, and travel to Brazil is at your own cost — budget for it before applying.

items.title: Goldman Sachs 10,000 Women India — 2026 Cohort
items.org: Goldman Sachs with IIM Ahmedabad, IIM Bangalore and IIM Lucknow
items.summary: A free, IIM-taught growth programme for established women business owners, covering finance, marketing, negotiation and leadership over three residential modules. It suits founders who already have a running business and want to scale it, not idea-stage startups.
eligibility: Woman owner or co-owner who is the primary decision-maker of the business
Business operating for at least one year
Annual turnover of about ₹30 lakh or more
