At least three employees
Open to all industries; previous 10,000 Women graduates cannot reapply
benefits: Tuition fully paid by Goldman Sachs for a 100+ hour executive-education programme
Three in-person residential modules taught by IIM faculty
Business mentoring from industry experts
Entry into an alumnae network of 4,000+ Indian women business owners and the global 10,000 Women community
items.note: The official page says applications close in November 2026, with interviews and decisions also in November and the cohort starting in December; aggregators list 30 Nov as the last date, so submit as early as you can. Applying starts with a 2-minute expression-of-interest form. Travel and lodging for the residential weeks are not covered. A free online version via Coursera exists for those who cannot attend in person.

items.title: Aerospace & Defence Acceleration Fund
items.org: IIMA Ventures (IIM Ahmedabad) with Jaivel Aerospace
items.amount: Up to US$400,000 (≈ ₹3.5 crore) per startup
items.summary: A balance-sheet fund from IIMA Ventures and Jaivel Aerospace that writes pre-seed and seed cheques of up to US$400K into Indian aerospace, defence and space-tech startups, paired with hands-on engineering mentorship and access to Jaivel's manufacturing network. It aims to back roughly 8–10 companies, so it suits founders seeking a first institutional round rather than a grant.
eligibility: Pre-seed or seed-stage startup, typically raising its first institutional cheque
Registered in India, or actively incorporating an Indian entity
Working on aerospace, defence or space-tech with dual-use potential — e.g. autonomy, propulsion, AI, high-performance materials, advanced manufacturing or secure communications
Credible plan for export scale and measurable national impact
Founding team willing to engage closely with mentors and industry partners
benefits: Pre-seed/seed investment of up to US$400,000 per selected startup
Technical and product mentorship from aerospace engineering, design and manufacturing leaders
Access to development facilities and Jaivel Aerospace's global manufacturing network
Industry partnerships and pilot opportunities with defence and aerospace players
items.note: No closing date is published — the fund accepts applications on an ongoing basis through the Typeform linked on the IIMA Ventures page. This is investment, not a grant: expect equity or an equity-linked instrument on early-stage terms, with the stake fixed after due diligence. Keep a technical deck, IP/patent status, prototype test data and cap table ready.

items.title: Women's Economic Empowerment Programme
items.org: IIMA Ventures (IIM Ahmedabad), supported by the Gates Foundation
items.amount: US$50,000+ per startup, plus up to US$250K cloud credits
items.summary: A year-long, Gates Foundation-backed IIMA Ventures programme for technology startups that raise the incomes of low-income Indian women — SHG members, women farmers, informal workers, gig and care-economy workers. Selected startups get milestone-linked funding of US$50K or more, pilots with partner organisations and fundraising support.
eligibility: Building a technology solution that measurably increases income for low-income women in India
Focus on rural SHG women and women farmers, informal workers and micro-entrepreneurs, gig/service-sector women, or care and domestic work
You can apply before incorporating, but must be a registered Indian entity before selection is confirmed
Startups from other accelerators may apply but must disclose prior support
Must take part in programme activities and an external impact-measurement study
No need to be based in Ahmedabad
benefits: Financial support of US$50,000 or more, released in milestone-linked tranches
Pilot and scale-up opportunities with market partners
Up to US$250,000 in cloud credits plus payment-gateway support
Access to customer, technology, policy and industry experts
Showcases, demo days, investor introductions and fundraising help through to deal closure
Training, mentoring and check-ins for up to a year
items.note: Rolling intake via IIMA Ventures' general application form (go.iimaventures.com/WebsiteForm). Catch: startups onboarded as incubatees are expected to give IIMA Ventures 2–5% mentoring equity. This is separate from the AI for Livelihoods Hackathon, which closes on 19 November 2026.

items.title: Bharat Inclusion Initiative
items.org: IIMA Ventures (IIM Ahmedabad), supported by the Gates Foundation and Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
items.summary: IIMA Ventures' long-running programme for fintech, skilling and livelihood startups whose customers include lower-income Indians (roughly under ₹50,000 a month). Selected startups receive US$50K or more in milestone-based support, plus pilots, mentoring and investor access for up to a year.
eligibility: Technology startup in fintech, skilling or livelihoods
At least part of your customers or beneficiaries must be lower-income households (typically earning under ₹50,000/month)
Idea to post-MVP stage — prototype, MVP and early-traction teams are preferred
Must be a registered Indian entity before selection is confirmed (not needed to apply)
Willing to participate in programme activities and an impact-measurement study
Alumni of other accelerators may apply; no need to be in Ahmedabad
benefits: US$50,000 or more per startup, disbursed in tranches against milestones
Possible additional grant or convertible-debt funding (not guaranteed)
Market access for pilots and scale-up, including DPI rails like ONDC, Account Aggregator, OCEN and ULI
Expert access on customers, regulation and industry
Demo days, corporate showcases and fundraising support
Cloud credits, partner offers and up to a year of mentoring
items.note: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis via go.iimaventures.com/WebsiteForm; IIMA Ventures says to expect an update within about a month. Catch: selected startups are onboarded as incubatees with 3–5% mentoring equity expected, and funds flow under a milestone-linked service agreement.

items.title: Bharat ClimateTech Initiative
items.summary: A two-year IIMA Ventures and MUFG programme that backs up to eight early-stage Indian climate-tech startups with up to ₹40 lakh each, plus mentoring and investor connections. It targets pre-seed to seed teams building or validating tech-enabled climate mitigation or resilience solutions.
eligibility: Startup registered and operating in India
Pre-seed to seed stage, developing or validating a tech-enabled solution
Working on climate, sustainability or related impact areas — e.g. decarbonisation, waste-to-value, climate tracking, climate finance or alternative fuels
benefits: Financial support of up to ₹40 lakh per startup
Mentoring from climate and sector experts
Market and investor connections
Cloud credits and service-provider offers
Support over a two-year programme for a small cohort (up to eight startups)
items.note: The official page shows an open 'Apply Now' form (go.iimaventures.com/WebsiteForm) but no closing date; listings describe it as rolling. Equity terms are not published — IIMA Ventures' other incubation programmes ask for 2–5% mentoring equity, so confirm before accepting. With only about eight slots, apply with pilot or emissions-impact data if you have it.

items.title: Keeling Curve Prize 2027
items.org: Climate Curve (US non-profit, formerly Global Warming Mitigation Project)
items.summary: An annual global climate prize that awards US$50,000 to each of ten projects already cutting, removing or replacing greenhouse-gas emissions, across five categories: Carbon Sinks, Energy, Finance, Social & Cultural Pathways, and Transport & Mobility. Startups, non-profits, research groups and intrapreneurs from India can apply.
eligibility: Open worldwide (except US-sanctioned jurisdictions) — Indian applicants are eligible
Startups, non-profits, university research groups, community leaders and intrapreneurs inside larger organisations can apply
Project must already be active and producing measurable emissions reductions or removals — pure ideas are not accepted
Must quantify the climate impact and explain how the project scales
Application in English with every question answered; past winners may re-enter only with a new project
benefits: US$50,000 unrestricted prize for each of the ten winners
Global visibility and networking with climate funders
Possible follow-on funding interest
Access to Climate Curve's fellowship programme (up to three interns per semester)
items.note: Closes 15 January 2027 at 11:59 PM UTC-12 (5:29 PM IST on 16 January) — or earlier once 500 eligible applications arrive, so apply early. Apply on kcp-conduit.org; upload all supporting documents before submitting, as nothing is accepted afterwards. No application fee.

items.title: RKVY-RAFTAAR Saranya Grant — Cohort 13
items.org: NEATEHUB (North East Agriculture Technology Entrepreneurs Hub), Jorhat, under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare's RKVY-RAFTAAR scheme
items.summary: A non-dilutive government grant of up to ₹25 lakh for agri and allied-sector startups that already have a working product with real users, paid in three milestone-linked tranches over 12–18 months. Run by NEATEHUB in Assam but open to DPIIT startups from anywhere in India, and you don't have to relocate.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup incorporated less than 7 years ago
Working MVP or pilot with real users and data — idea-stage ventures are not the target
Must operate in agriculture or an allied sector; pure trading, distribution or service businesses without an innovation core are excluded
Majority of equity held by Indian citizens (OCI founders are allowed)
Revenue-generating, ideally ₹10 lakh+ ARR; applicants should meet at least four of the five quick-check criteria
Operations or pilots in North-East India score extra but are not mandatory
benefits: Grant-in-aid of up to ₹25 lakh with no equity taken
Funds released in three tranches tied to a milestone plan agreed in the first week
Dedicated go-to-market mentorship and technical guidance
Access to NEATEHUB's institutional and follow-on investor networks
Non-residential programme — only committee pitches and the valedictory session are in Jorhat
items.note: Applications opened 9 Nov 2026 and close 30 Nov 2026; they are reviewed on a rolling basis, so earlier is better. Apply via NEATEHUB's Accubate form linked on the programme page. Budget for travel to Jorhat for the committee pitch.

items.title: FinTech Innovation Lab New York — 2027 Class
items.org: FinTech Innovation Lab (Partnership Fund for New York City with Accenture)
items.amount: Non-dilutive; pairing with 3–6 global financial institutions
items.summary: A free, 12-week hybrid programme in New York (March–June 2027) that pairs B2B fintech startups with senior executives at three to six of the 40+ participating banks, insurers and asset managers to work towards paid pilots. No equity, no fees, and non-US startups — including Indian ones — can apply.
eligibility: Early- or growth-stage company with at least a beta product; typically pre-seed to Series B
Building technology relevant to financial-services institutions (B2B fintech, insurtech, cyber, data/AI for banks)
Open to companies from any country, but the core team must be able to attend in-person sessions in New York and arrange its own US visas
Pilot Track applicants must be growth-stage with a production-ready product
benefits: Mentorship and pairing with 3–6 financial institutions, each with an executive sponsor and a day-to-day contact
Access to the Lab's network of 40+ banks, insurers and asset managers
Pilot Track: proof-of-concept support with Accenture's Innovation Garage
Cohorts of about 10 companies typically start 20–40 proofs of concept
No equity taken and no application or participation fee
items.note: Applications close 25 Nov 2026 (US time — submit by 24 Nov evening IST to be safe) via portal.fintechinnovationlab.com. Notifications mid-January; Shark Tank Day 2 Feb and Finalist Demo Fair 4 Feb 2027. Catch: the Lab does not sponsor visas or reimburse travel, and core team members must be in New York for in-person sessions during the programme.

items.title: AppWorks Accelerator #34 (AW#34)
items.amount: Free programme; no equity or fees
items.summary: A free three-month accelerator run by AppWorks, one of Asia's largest founder networks, that takes no equity, tokens, revenue share or fees. Founders from anywhere can apply to join a community of 650+ startups across nine Asian markets, with Taipei as the main base.
eligibility: Founders operating from anywhere in the world can apply (contact the team to confirm fit for India-based startups)
Early-stage startups with a team and product direction; AppWorks focuses on AI, Web3, IoT and tech businesses targeting Asian markets
Willingness to take part in a hybrid online/offline programme, with in-person participation in Taipei encouraged
Apply through the AW#34 Typeform application
benefits: Three-month programme with mentorship and a founder community that continues afterwards
Access to 650+ startups and mentors across Asia
Connections to 25+ venture funds and corporate partners
Help with Taiwan Gold Card / Entrepreneur Visa and company setup
No equity, tokens, options, revenue share, rent or service fees
items.note: Two rounds: first round closes 29 Nov 2026, final round closes 27 Dec 2026 — earlier applicants have a better admission chance. AppWorks does not commit to investing; fundraising is discussed separately. Expect travel to Taipei for in-person sessions.

items.title: AIMM 2026 — AI for Manufacturing and Mankind Challenge
items.org: MAGIC (Marathwada Accelerator for Growth and Incubation Council), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
items.summary: The eighth edition of MAGIC's national AI innovation contest, with ₹7 lakh in cash prizes for AI solutions to industrial and social problems. It has two tracks — MVP/proof-of-concept ideas and revenue-generating products — and winners can also get seed-funding support and incubation at MAGIC.
eligibility: Open nationally to startups, new entrepreneurs, MSMEs, students and research teams
Solution must use AI to solve a manufacturing, industrial or societal problem
Category 1: concepts at MVP stage with a working proof of concept
Category 2: AI products already in the market and generating revenue
benefits: Share of ₹7 lakh total cash prizes
Seed-funding support for eligible winning innovations
Incubation opportunity with MAGIC, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Exposure to MAGIC's industry network in the Marathwada manufacturing cluster
items.note: Applications close 7 Dec 2026 (closing time not published — submit a day early). The organiser's application link is the short link above; prize split per category and the finale date had not been published at launch, so check the form for details. Pick the right category: idea-stage entries must already show a proof of concept.

items.title: Grand Startup Challenge 2026
items.org: CARS24, with Startup India, MeitY Startup Hub and the Startup Policy Forum
items.summary: A national challenge for early-stage Indian startups working on fintech and lending, mobility and road safety, logistics and supply chains, or sovereign AI. Shortlisted teams get a month of mentoring in December before pitching at a finale in New Delhi in January 2027, where winners share a ₹1 crore prize pool.
eligibility: Startup incorporated in India as a Private Limited Company or LLP
At least one founder working on the company full time
Early-stage: startups that have already raised more than ₹50 crore are excluded
Product must fit one of the four tracks: fintech/lending, mobility & road safety, logistics & supply chain, or sovereign AI
Must pass eight yes/no screening questions at the start of the form
benefits: Share of a ₹1 crore prize pool split across winners in all four tracks
Mentorship month in December 2026 for shortlisted startups
Pitch and demo slot at the January 2027 finale in New Delhi
Visibility to investors and the partner organisations
items.note: Applications close 20 Nov 2026 at 11:59 PM IST (already extended once). The form takes about 30 minutes and needs a pitch deck PDF (max 50 MB) plus a 2–5 minute founder video link (YouTube, Drive or Loom). Two reviewers score track fit, product evidence, team and traction equally. Per-winner prize split and any equity terms are not published.

items.title: Create AI Agents Championship (Dubai)
items.org: Dubai Chamber of Digital Economy (Create Apps in Dubai initiative)
items.amount: AED 550,000 grant per category winner; AED 1M 'AI Agent of the Year'
items.summary: A Dubai government-backed global contest for AI agents, with four categories (societal, personal, business and youth). Each category winner gets an AED 550,000 development grant and one is named 'AI Agent of the Year' with AED 1 million; the total pool is over AED 2.5 million.
eligibility: Open to innovators worldwide, technical or non-technical, as individuals or teams
Entries can be at idea, prototype or early-MVP stage; fully commercialised products are not eligible
Startups and existing companies may enter a new AI-agent solution or capability
Youth category: lead applicant must be under 21 at registration
Entry needs an AI-agent prototype, a pitch deck and a demo video
benefits: AED 550,000 grant for each of the Societal, Personal, Business and Youth category winners
AED 1 million and the 'AI Agent of the Year' title for one overall winner
Introductory agentic-AI workshops plus a Digital Academy with advanced courses, practical workshops and mentoring
Visibility through a championship launched by Dubai's Crown Prince
items.note: Launched 7 Oct 2026; organisers say registration closes in December 2026 but have not published the exact day, so 31 Dec is a placeholder — submit early and check the site. The announcements do not mention entry fees or equity, and how the AED 1M award combines with the category grant is not spelled out. Sources: WAM announcement as carried by Khaleej Times and Gulf Today.

items.title: BIRAC Call for Proposals under Femtech (2026)
items.org: BIRAC (Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council), Department of Biotechnology
items.summary: BIRAC has opened a dedicated call for women-led Indian startups building products for women's health — from menstrual and reproductive care to maternal health, gynaecological cancer diagnostics and menopause. Selected startups are offered investment support along with technology and market linkages through BIRAC's network.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised Indian startup registered as a private limited company or LLP
At least 51% of shares held by resident Indian citizens
A woman founder, co-founder or CXO must hold a key role in the company

Product must address women's health: reproductive, sexual or menstrual health; maternal and prenatal care; diagnostics and breast/gynaecological cancer; digital health, AI or mental health for women; or menopause and hormonal health
Early-stage through scale-up companies can apply
benefits: Investment support from BIRAC (instrument and size decided per proposal)
Technology and market linkages through BIRAC's ecosystem
Committee-led evaluation with feedback on technical merit
items.note: Last date 23 Nov 2026 (BIRAC homepage notice; no closing time given, so submit by the evening of 22 Nov). Apply through the BIRAC portal and download the Femtech guidelines and flyer from the BIRAC homepage first. The amount and investment terms are not stated publicly — read the guidelines carefully for any equity conditions before applying. Keep your DPIIT certificate, incorporation documents and cap table ready.

items.title: KSUM BCDD Startup Grant (Idea + Productisation)
items.org: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM) with the Backward Classes Development Department, Government of Kerala
items.amount: Up to ₹10 lakh total (Idea grant up to ₹3 lakh + Productisation grant)
items.summary: A Kerala government grant, run through KSUM, that backs technology startups founded by graduates from the OBC/OEC communities. Founders can draw an Idea grant of up to ₹3 lakh and then a Productisation grant to turn a prototype into a market-ready product, with total support capped at ₹10 lakh and released in milestone-linked tranches.
eligibility: Founder must be a graduate (any stream) from the OBC/OEC category, aged 23 to 40
Founder/innovator's annual income must be below ₹5 lakh
OBC/OEC founders must together hold at least 80% of the company's shares
Must be building an innovative technology-driven product (service projects, asset purchases and CSR activities are not funded)
Idea grant: innovators based in or outside Kerala may apply
Productisation grant: company must already be incorporated and hold a KSUM Unique ID
benefits: Idea grant of up to ₹3 lakh for prototyping and validation
Productisation grant towards making the product market-ready, within the ₹10 lakh overall cap
Milestone-based funding with KSUM monitoring and mentoring
Entry into the Kerala Startup Mission ecosystem and its programmes
items.note: Rolling — the official KSUM grants portal shows the call as open with no closing date. Apply online on grants.startupmission.in; shortlisted founders pitch to an expert committee and incomplete forms are rejected. Company incorporation (Pvt Ltd, LLP or OPC) and a KSUM Unique ID are mandatory before any money is released. You cannot outsource the whole product build or a major milestone. Read the BCDD guidelines PDF on the portal for the exact Productisation cap and the document list before applying.

items.title: ELEVATE NxT 2026–27 (DeepTech)
items.org: Startup Karnataka, Dept. of Electronics, IT, BT & S&T, Government of Karnataka
items.summary: Karnataka's deep-tech track of its ELEVATE grant programme gives milestone-linked grants of up to ₹1 crore to technology startups between TRL 3 and TRL 8. Startups from anywhere in India can apply, but winners must shift their registered office to Karnataka.
eligibility: Private limited company, registered partnership, LLP or cooperative society; not a subsidiary, spin-off or internal division
Incorporated within the last 20 years, with turnover below ₹300 crore in every financial year
At least two founding or core team members
Must not have received an ELEVATE grant in the previous three years
Genuine deep-tech product at Technology Readiness Level 3–8, with a short write-up justifying the deep-tech claim
Non-Karnataka entities that win must move their registered office to Karnataka within four months of results
benefits: Equity-free grant-in-aid of up to ₹1 crore, paid in milestone tranches
Incubation and mentoring linkages through Karnataka's government-backed startup network
items.note: Window opened 13 Oct 2026; the official portal now shows the last date as 14 Dec 2026, 5:00 PM IST (launch-day press coverage said 13 Nov, so the window appears extended). Apply only on the ELEVATE portal; you may also apply to ELEVATE Minorities if eligible. Helpline: startupcell@karnataka.gov.in / 080-22231007.

items.title: ELEVATE Minorities 2026
items.summary: A dedicated ELEVATE call that awards one-time grants of up to ₹50 lakh to Karnataka startups majority-owned by founders from notified minority communities. Selected startups also get subsidised incubation and mentoring.
eligibility: Incorporated in Karnataka as a private limited company, OPC, registered partnership, LLP or cooperative society
No more than 10 years old, with turnover under ₹200 crore
At least one director/partner from a minority community (Muslim, Christian, Buddhist, Jain, Sikh or Parsi), with minority members holding at least 51% equity throughout the project
That director/partner needs a valid digital minority certificate with an RD number from the Karnataka Revenue Department
No ELEVATE grant in the previous three years
benefits: Non-repayable, equity-free grant of up to ₹50 lakh released against milestones
Subsidised incubation and mentoring through Karnataka government-backed incubators
items.note: Last date per the official portal: 14 Dec 2026, 5:00 PM IST (originally announced as 13 Nov). Selection includes an in-person pitch where the majority-holding minority director/partner must attend. Keep a CA-certified shareholding pattern and the digital RD-numbered certificate ready.

items.title: MSInS IPR Support Scheme
items.org: Maharashtra State Innovation Society (MSInS), Government of Maharashtra
items.amount: 100% reimbursement: up to ₹5 lakh domestic / ₹20 lakh international
items.summary: Under the Maharashtra Startup, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Policy 2025, MSInS reimburses the full eligible cost (excluding taxes) of securing patents, industrial designs and software copyrights. Fresh guidelines were notified in October 2026 with caps of ₹5 lakh for domestic and ₹20 lakh for international IP.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup incorporated or registered in Maharashtra with real operations in the state
Turnover within ₹5 crore for domestic claims, or within ₹100 crore for international claims
Claim after the patent is granted or the design/software copyright is registered
Trademarks, geographical indications, plant varieties and literary/artistic works are not covered
benefits: Reimbursement of 100% of eligible IP costs (excluding GST), up to ₹5 lakh domestic and ₹20 lakh international per applicant
Covers patents, industrial design registration and software/code copyright
items.note: Rolling reimbursement claim; MSInS verifies documents and pays directly to the bank account. Guidelines issued 9 Oct 2026 by the Skill Development, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Dept. Individual innovators who are ITI or skill-university students/alumni have separate claim rules. Keep grant/registration certificates and paid invoices ready.

items.title: Goa Startup Seed Capital Grant
items.org: Startup & IT Promotion Cell (SITPC), Dept. of IT, Electronics & Communications, Government of Goa
items.summary: Goa's flagship startup grant offers a one-time award of up to ₹10 lakh to SITPC-certified startups that have built a promising minimum viable product. Applications are screened by an expert committee and approved by an empowered committee chaired by the Chief Minister.
eligibility: Startup certified by Goa's Startup & IT Promotion Cell
Has a working minimum viable product (or a clear plan to build one) to present to the expert panel
Directors' bank accounts linked to Aadhaar; Goa office address proof
Up to 100 startups can be supported per year
benefits: One-time, non-dilutive grant of up to ₹10 lakh
Pitch opportunity before the state's expert and empowered committees
items.note: Rolling; applications are batched for periodic expert-committee meetings (a June 2026 round funded 15 of 26 applicants). Documents: Goa address proof, cancelled cheque, founder CV in World Bank format, and a pitch to the expert panel. All awards are discretionary.

items.title: Goa Startup IPR (Patent) Reimbursement
items.org: Startup & IT Promotion Cell (SITPC), Government of Goa
items.amount: Up to ₹2 lakh national / ₹5 lakh international
items.summary: Goa reimburses up to the full cost of protecting a startup's intellectual property, capped at ₹2 lakh for national and ₹5 lakh for international filings. It is listed as its own incentive under the Goa Startup Policy.
eligibility: SITPC-certified Goa startup
IP must relate to a technology-based product or service, with government and attorney fees already paid
One claim per IP; not already claimed under any other central or state scheme
Aadhaar-linked director bank accounts and digital payments
benefits: Reimbursement of up to 100% of IP filing and related costs
Caps of ₹2 lakh (national) and ₹5 lakh (international); up to 200 startups per year
items.note: Rolling post-expense claim; payout depends on available budget and SITPC recommendation. Submit the IP filing/registration copy, invoices, payment proofs, an expense statement and a short report. A separate trademark reimbursement (50%, up to ₹25,000) also exists.

items.title: MP Startup Investment Assistance
items.org: MP Start-up Centre / MSME Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh
items.amount: 15% of funds raised, up to ₹15 lakh per stage (₹18 lakh for women-led)
items.summary: Madhya Pradesh tops up external funding raised by its startups with a state grant equal to 15% of each investment, up to ₹15 lakh per round for up to four rounds. Women-led startups get 18%, up to ₹18 lakh per round.
eligibility: Startup established in Madhya Pradesh and registered on the MP startup portal (DPIIT recognition)
Investment or loan must come from a SEBI-registered investor/AIF, RBI-recognised financial institution or scheduled bank
Loans must have a repayment tenure of at least one year
Can be claimed for a maximum of four funding stages
benefits: Grant of 15% of each eligible investment, up to ₹15 lakh per stage and ₹60 lakh lifetime
Women-led startups: 18%, up to ₹18 lakh per stage and ₹72 lakh overall
items.note: Rolling, under the MP Startup Policy and Implementation Scheme 2025 (five-year policy). The incubator named in the application gets a share of the first-phase assistance. The portal also lists SC/ST-led startups for the higher rate, while the policy PDF names women-led only, so confirm before claiming.

items.title: MP Startup Patent Assistance
items.org: MP Start-up Centre / MSME Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh
items.summary: Madhya Pradesh reimburses actual patent expenditure of up to ₹5 lakh for startups established in the state. It is a separate assistance line in the MP Startup Policy 2025.
eligibility: Startup established in Madhya Pradesh and registered on the MP startup portal
Patent must have been obtained for the startup
Claim covers actual expenditure incurred on the patent
DPIIT recognition required for portal registration
benefits: Reimbursement of actual patent costs up to ₹5 lakh
Can be combined with other MP startup policy incentives such as lease rental and investment assistance
items.note: Rolling reimbursement after the patent is obtained; apply through the MP startup portal with the state application form. Keep the patent certificate and paid invoices ready.

items.title: Himachal CM Startup/Innovation Projects Scheme – Sustenance Allowance
items.org: Department of Industries, Government of Himachal Pradesh
items.summary: Himachal's Chief Minister's Startup/Innovation Projects/New Industries Scheme pays innovators a monthly allowance of ₹25,000 for one year. To qualify, an empanelled host incubator has to recommend the project and the state Empowered Committee has to approve it. Selected innovators also get free mentoring and lab access at the incubator for up to 3 years (service startups) or 5 years (product startups).
eligibility: Any individual or group with an innovative idea or concept
The project must be recommended by an empanelled host institution or incubation centre in Himachal (e.g. IIT Mandi, NIT Hamirpur, HPU, IIM Sirmaur)
The Empowered Committee under the Directorate of Industries must approve the project
Monthly progress reports are needed to keep receiving the allowance
benefits: ₹25,000 a month for 12 months, paid directly to the innovator
Free incubation, mentoring and lab access at the host institution
Marketing help and seed/angel support may follow on the incubator's recommendation once the product is ready to commercialise
items.note: Rolling: the portal shows registration as open and lists no closing date. Process: register online and get a tracking number, then the Department of Industries scrutiny committee checks the application. Next, get a recommendation from an empanelled incubator (the committee decides within about 20 days), and the institution sends the proposal to the Directorate. No application fee. The portal lists the HIMSUP seed fund (up to ₹50 lakh) as a separate benefit, but it opens in rounds (the last one closed in Dec 2025), so it is not included here. Contact: startuphimachal@gmail.com, 0177-2622735.

items.title: Sikkim Start-up Policy 2025 – One-time Establishment Grant
items.org: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Sikkim
items.summary: Sikkim's Start-up Policy 2025 (notified 9 Oct 2025 and valid for five years) offers a one-time grant of up to ₹1 lakh to startups based in Sikkim. The grant covers setting up the business, marketing and early running costs. Startups claim it after getting a Spark ID on the state's SPARK portal.
eligibility: At least 51% of the equity must be held by Sikkim-origin founders with a valid Certificate of Identification (or the startup must be DPIIT-recognised with 51% Sikkim-origin ownership)
Incorporated no more than 10 years ago (15 for biotech), with turnover of ₹100 crore or less in every year
Must be a private limited company, OPC, registered partnership or LLP working on a scalable, technology- or IP-led innovation
Must not be a spin-off or reconstruction of an existing family business
Must have a Spark ID from the Sikkim SPARK portal
benefits: Up to ₹1 lakh one-time grant for establishment, marketing and recurring costs
Opens access to other policy benefits such as patent, certification, marketing and R&D lab reimbursements
items.note: The policy is in force (gazetted 10 Nov 2025) and has no closing date, but the detailed SOP and claim forms are issued separately, so confirm the claim route with the Commerce & Industries Department before applying. The policy's seed fund (up to ₹10–15 lakh) waits on its own SOP and the annual challenge grants (₹4 lakh / ₹2 lakh) run in rounds, so neither is listed as open. Benefits stop if Sikkim-origin ownership falls below 26%.

items.title: Sikkim Start-up Policy 2025 – Incubator/Co-working Rent Reimbursement
items.org: Commerce & Industries Department, Government of Sikkim
items.amount: 50% of rent, up to ₹2.5 lakh/year for 3 years
items.summary: Under Sikkim's 2025 startup policy, eligible startups get back half of the rent they pay to incubators or co-working spaces inside Sikkim. The cap is ₹2.5 lakh a year, for up to three years.
eligibility: Sikkim-origin startup under the policy definition (51% Sikkim-origin ownership with a COI, or DPIIT-recognised with the same ownership)
Must have a Spark ID from the Sikkim SPARK portal
Rent must be paid to an incubator or co-working space located in Sikkim
Within 10 years of incorporation (15 for biotech), with turnover of ₹100 crore or less
benefits: 50% reimbursement of rent paid
Up to ₹2.5 lakh a year for up to 3 years (₹7.5 lakh in total)
items.note: Paid back against rent already paid, so keep the lease agreement and rent receipts. The policy is valid for 5 years from Oct 2025 with no application window, but the department issues the claim procedure separately, so check the SPARK portal or department first.

items.title: Startup Punjab Seed Grant
items.org: Department of Industries & Commerce, Government of Punjab (Startup Punjab)
items.summary: Punjab gives early-stage, DPIIT-recognised startups a seed grant for idea validation, prototype building, market research, travel, training and initial setup. The money is routed through recognised incubators. In June 2026 the state handed out ₹1.07 crore to 31 startups: 7 of them received the revised ₹5 lakh grant and 24 received ₹3 lakh.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup that is based, incubated or operating in Punjab
Registered with the Startup Punjab cell
Private limited company, registered partnership or LLP, under 10 years old with turnover below ₹100 crore
Must apply through a state- or centre-recognised incubator
benefits: Seed grant of up to ₹3 lakh under the earlier policy, raised to ₹5 lakh under the 2026 policy
Can be used for prototyping, validation, market research, marketing, skill training and setup costs
items.note: Rolling, routed through incubators, and has no published window. Get DPIIT recognition, register with Startup Punjab, join a recognised incubator, then file the claim (Invest Punjab / fasttrack.punjab.gov.in). The ₹5 lakh figure comes from June 2026 news coverage of the Industrial & Business Development Policy 2026 (notified 8 Mar 2026). The Startup India state page still shows ₹3 lakh. An aggregator mentions a second tranche of up to ₹10 lakh for 20 startups a year, but no official text confirms it.

items.title: Women Startup Program, Cohort 6 (Entrepreneurship Base Program)
items.amount: Up to ₹10 lakh grant per selected venture
items.summary: Cohort 6 of NSRCEL's women-founder programme is now a two-year track that starts with a 5-week foundations module, then 2 months of pre-incubation and 8 months of incubation. Selected ventures can receive a ₹10 lakh grant. Right now only the entry-level Entrepreneurship Base Program is taking applications.
eligibility: Women entrepreneurs aged 18 or older with a workable business idea (Entrepreneurship Base Program)
Solo founders accepted; open to any sector
For the incubation stage: India-based, woman-majority-owned venture that is MVP-ready or in early growth, with early revenue or strong market validation and a 12-month revenue projection
benefits: Grant of up to ₹10 lakh for selected ventures, based on eligibility criteria
Mentoring, need assessment, and cohort-based learning
Free legal and company-secretarial advice, plus co-incubation with partner institutes
Showcase events and support to scale after the programme
items.note: The page shows no closing date; only the Entrepreneurship Base Program is marked open, and the Incubation and Scale Hub tracks say 'coming soon'. Apply through the Kotak BizLabs Accubate form linked from the page. The separate expression-of-interest form does not count as an application. Participation is mostly free and NSRCEL takes no equity. Queries: wspqueries@iimb.ac.in.

items.title: Impact Orbit – AgeTech Innovations
items.amount: Grants up to ₹12.5 lakh for select ventures
items.summary: An 8–9 month impact programme, funded by Capgemini's CSR, for ventures that serve older adults. It covers preventive care, home care, mobility aids, financial and legal security, and social wellbeing. Select ventures can receive grants of up to ₹12.5 lakh.
eligibility: Registered for-profit or non-profit entity that has operated for at least 1 year
At least one full-time founder and at least 3 employees
Early traction or early customers (MVP or post-MVP); idea-stage teams are directed to NSRCEL Launchpad
Impact-first venture that can contribute to at least 3 UN SDGs
benefits: Grants of up to ₹12.5 lakh for select ventures (not guaranteed)
One-on-one mentoring and fundraising readiness
Support on legal compliance, impact measurement, and leadership
Help using technology to scale
items.note: The page says 'Applications are now open!' and gives no closing date. Apply through the online form (pitch deck required) linked from the page. Selection: internal review, then a 6–7 minute pitch to an external panel, then due diligence. No fees and no equity.

items.title: Circular Bharat Accelerator
items.org: NSRCEL, IIM Bangalore with HUL, NITI Aayog and Xynteo
items.amount: Milestone-based grants for select pilot-ready startups (amount not stated)
items.summary: An accelerator under Hindustan Unilever's Project Circular Bharat for circular-economy startups that are ready to pilot. Focus areas include plastics and packaging, advanced recycling, reuse and refill models, e-waste, and next-generation textiles. Select ventures receive milestone-based grants and access to corporate pilots.
eligibility: Tech-enabled, circularity-focused venture incorporated in India
Operating for at least 1 year (the FAQ also says under 10 years old, with 50 or fewer staff)
Market-ready product with early revenue and pilot readiness (TRL 5 or above)
benefits: Milestone-based grants for select pilot-ready startups
Go-to-market and pilot-readiness support, plus roundtables with corporates and policymakers
One-on-one mentoring, VC connections, and long-term alumni access
items.note: The NSRCEL homepage lists this programme as open, and the programme page has an active 'Apply Now' button but no closing date. The 'Register Your Interest' form is not the full application. Selection: screening, jury evaluation, then due diligence. Free, and no equity is taken. The grant size is not published.

items.title: Healthcare Incubation Program
items.amount: Up to ₹1 crore grant for a few select startups
items.summary: A five-month hybrid incubation programme for healthcare startups, run with DailyRounds. It covers healthtech, medtech, biotech, affordable public health, and chronic and elderly care. By the end, a few select startups can receive grants of up to ₹1 crore.
eligibility: Healthcare startup at prototype to early-revenue stage with a working prototype or proof of concept
Open to startups across India; solo founders accepted
Founders must be committed full-time
Only one idea per applicant
benefits: Grants of up to ₹1 crore for a few top startups at the end of the programme
Mentoring and clinical and industry connections through DailyRounds
No participation fee
items.note: The page says 'Applications are now open' and gives no closing date. Apply through the form linked on the page. Equity terms are not mentioned, so confirm before signing. Only a few startups receive the ₹1 crore grant.

items.title: TiHAN Call for Startup Proposals (Autonomous Navigation)
items.summary: A rolling call from IIT Hyderabad's Technology Innovation Hub on Autonomous Navigation. It funds startups for 12 months to build autonomous ground, aerial, and water systems and related technology. Examples include AI navigation, V2X communications, edge computing, swarm coordination, and monitoring for agriculture, defence, and infrastructure.
eligibility: Indian company with at least 51% Indian ownership
Recognised under the DPIIT startup policy (pre-registration is allowed)
Incubated at a government-supported technology park or incubator
Valid balance sheets and supporting documents
benefits: Up to ₹15 lakh in project funding over 12 months
Access to the TiHAN autonomous-navigation testbed ecosystem at IIT Hyderabad
items.note: The page says applications are accepted on a rolling basis ('Rolling Advertisement'). Submit the proposal in the Annexure A format as one PDF with proof of registration and balance sheets, through the 'Apply Now' form. The page text says Google Form but the link goes to Microsoft Forms. Queries: office.tihan@iith.ac.in. The page does not state equity or IP terms.

items.title: CV Labs Co-creation Workshop
items.amount: Up to ₹7 lakh research prototype grant
items.summary: A two-week co-creation workshop where startups work with IIIT Hyderabad research labs and faculty to build or improve a proof of concept. The recent edition focused on computer vision for industrial manufacturing. Startups can win a research prototype grant of up to ₹7 lakh.
eligibility: Startups building on emerging technology such as AI/ML, computer vision, NLP, or LLMs
The August 2026 edition targeted computer-vision solutions for industrial manufacturing
Product teams from large companies may also apply
benefits: Research prototype grant of up to ₹7 lakh
Lectures and one-on-one mentoring from IIITH faculty and research labs
A route into RootNode, CIE's longer research-advisory programme
items.note: Runs quarterly with domain-specific editions. The page has an open 'Apply now' Google Form and no closing date, and CIE's August 2026 newsletter listed it as a current call. The next edition's dates and theme are not published, so confirm with CIE. Equity terms are not stated.

items.title: National Quantum Mission Startup Support (Rolling Call)
items.org: Department of Science & Technology (National Quantum Mission) via Thematic Hubs
items.amount: Up to ₹5 crore seed (Track 1); up to ₹25 crore (Track 2)
items.summary: DST's National Quantum Mission funds Indian quantum-technology startups through its four Thematic Hubs (computing, communication, sensing/metrology, materials/devices), with an application window that stays open year-round. Early-stage startups without VC money can get seed of up to ₹5 crore, and VC-backed startups can get up to ₹25 crore for scale-up.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup (funds are released only after recognition if it is still pending at application)
Indian company with IP held in India and Indian promoters owning at least 51%
Core product or service built on quantum technology in one of the four NQM domains
Track 1 is for startups with no VC funding yet; Track 2 is for startups that have raised one or more VC rounds
benefits: Slab A up to ₹1 crore (idea to proof of concept) and Slab B up to ₹5 crore (prototype, validation, pilots)
Slab C up to ₹25 crore for VC-backed startups, via CCPS or co-investment with a VC
Access to hub infrastructure, mentoring and academic partners at IISc, IIT Madras, IIT Bombay and IIT Delhi
items.note: This is equity, not a grant. The hub takes up to 3% (Slab A) or up to 4.5% total (Slab B) as an incubation fee, and Slab C is structured as CCPS at a 15–30% discount to the next round. Applications go to the Thematic Hub for your domain, through that hub's own portal. Evaluation covers pre-screening, a technical review with a pitch and an investment committee, and takes up to about 3 months. Funds are released in milestone tranches. The window is rolling and cohorts are reviewed quarterly.

items.title: GREAT Grant for Technical Textiles Startups (NTTM)
items.org: Ministry of Textiles – National Technical Textiles Mission
items.summary: The GREAT component of the National Technical Textiles Mission gives grant-in-aid of up to ₹50 lakh to help early-stage founders turn technical-textile ideas into prototypes or commercial products. In July 2026 the Ministry said 31 startups had been approved so far and that the scheme remains open to eligible startups nationwide.
eligibility: Individual innovators, or startups registered as a private limited company, partnership firm or LLP, within the scheme's turnover limit
Must apply through an associated incubator and sign an agreement with it
Project must be at idea-to-MVP stage and aimed at a technical-textiles prototype or commercial product
Founder must put in a minimum own-funds contribution, as set in the guidelines
benefits: Grant of up to ₹50 lakh, with no equity taken by the government
Support for up to 18 months, paid in instalments against milestones
Incubator mentoring and lab access during the project
items.note: Applications go through the NTTM GREAT portal with a partner incubator. The last instalment is paid as a reimbursement, so plan for working capital. An aggregator reports a July 2026 office memorandum extending the window to 31 Dec 2027; this is not confirmed on an official page, so check the portal for the current window before applying.

items.title: DRDO Technology Development Fund (TDF) for Startups & MSMEs
items.amount: Grant up to 90% of project cost (startup projects typically up to ₹10 crore)
items.summary: DRDO's Technology Development Fund pays milestone-based grant-in-aid to Indian startups and MSMEs that build defence and dual-use technologies listed by the armed forces, covering up to 90% of project cost. Firms register on the TDF portal and then bid against specific technology RFPs as they are published.
eligibility: Indian startup or MSME: public or private limited company, partnership, LLP, OPC or registered sole proprietorship
Owned and controlled by resident Indian citizens, with no more than 49% foreign investment

Under the startup route: DPIIT-recognised, incorporated no more than 3 years before applying, and incubated at a Central or State government-supported incubator with a defence and aerospace track record
No prior government grant for a similar technology; academic and non-profit research bodies can join only as partners with an industry lead
benefits: Grant of up to 90% of project cost, released against milestones over a typical 2-year development period
Startup projects of up to ₹10 crore estimated cost, with up to 20% support available to the host incubator
Guidance from DRDO labs and a route to defence procurement
items.note: This is not one open call. You register on tdf.drdo.gov.in, verify your profile and then apply against technology-specific RFPs as they are posted, each with its own deadline. Check the portal's project list for live RFPs. The official scheme summary also mentions a higher overall project cap of ₹50 crore for some project types.

items.title: Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) – Azure Credits
items.summary: Microsoft's always-open startup programme gives software companies Azure credits that unlock in stages as they show real usage and progress, with the largest tier reserved for startups backed by a Microsoft Investor Network partner. Approved members also get go-to-market help, Marketplace/co-sell routes and, for some, a named Microsoft contact.
eligibility: Privately held, for-profit company building a software product or service it owns
Headquartered in a country where Azure is offered (India qualifies if it appears during Azure sign-up)
Has not raised Series C or later and has received under $350,000 in lifetime free Azure credits
Educational institutions, government bodies, consultancies/agencies and crypto-mining businesses are excluded
benefits: Azure credits of up to $150K, released progressively as usage and milestones are verified
Higher-value benefits earlier for startups with an Investor Network referral code
Go-to-market support, Microsoft Marketplace and co-sell opportunities, startup-specific Azure resources
items.note: Rolling; apply at startups.microsoft.com via 'Get started'. Needs a Microsoft account, legal company name matching incorporation papers, address and payment details, and personal LinkedIn verification. Decisions usually within about three business days. Without an investor referral code you start on a lower credit tier.

items.title: Mastercard Start Path
items.summary: Mastercard's roughly six-month virtual engagement programme connects funded, revenue-generating startups with Mastercard product teams, partners and customers to pilot and co-build commercial deals. Mastercard may take an option to invest in some participants, but investment is neither the aim nor guaranteed.
eligibility: Has raised outside investment (seed, Series A or later)
Product already live in market and generating revenue, with reference customers
Solution fits Mastercard's strategy, e.g. payments, digital assets, cybersecurity, sustainability or emerging tech
Open to startups from all regions, including India
benefits: Access to Mastercard's global network of issuers, merchants, partners and customers
Mentorship, co-innovation and dedicated pipeline/commercial support
Visibility and credibility from the Mastercard association, plus possible investment
items.note: Applications are taken online with no published window. Shortlisted startups are asked to share more with relevant product teams before selection. No fee is mentioned. Not for idea-stage teams: you need funding, revenue and a live product.

items.title: Cloudflare for Startups
items.summary: Cloudflare gives tech startups one year of credits for its developer platform, network and security products, from $10K for bootstrapped teams up to $350K for well-funded startups backed by an affiliated investor. Higher tiers add an account manager and solutions-architect office hours.
eligibility: Incorporated within the last 10 years, for-profit, actively building a technology product
Funded up to Series B, with funding raised in the last 12 months
Live public website and a public presence on LinkedIn, X or GitHub; business email matching the company domain
First-time applicants only; the $100K and $350K tiers need backing from an affiliated partner investor
benefits: Tier 3: $10K credits for bootstrapped/self-funded startups with under $1M raised
Tier 2: $100K and Tier 1: $350K for partner-backed startups, with an account manager and bi-weekly architect office hours at the top tier
items.note: Apply through the 'Apply here' link on the programme page. Review usually takes up to 48 hours, with approval by email. Credits expire after 12 months or when used up. The page does not list eligible countries, so confirm India-based billing works during sign-up.

items.title: Emergent Ventures India
items.summary: A low-overhead grant and fellowship programme backing ambitious 'zero to one' ideas, with a dedicated India tranche that announced its 20th India cohort in October 2026. It funds individuals and early projects in any field, including first steps toward a company.
eligibility: Open to individuals worldwide aged 13+; choose India under 'My Project Will Affect' to enter the India tranche
One application per applicant and project
Application must be written by the applicant: AI-written applications are screened out (proofreading only)
Best suited to bold, scalable ideas from talented individuals rather than mature businesses
benefits: Grant or fellowship money sized to the project, decided by a small team with little paperwork
Membership of the Emergent Ventures winners' network, with India cohorts publicly announced on Marginal Revolution
items.note: Rolling, with no deadline or batch. Use 'Apply Now' on the Mercatus page and select India in the drop-down. No feedback or status updates are given, and requests for them may go unanswered. Grant sizes are not published.

items.title: Hub71 Access Programme – Cohort 21 (incl. Hub71+ AI)
items.summary: Abu Dhabi's tech hub offers selected startups AED 250K of in-kind incentives (housing, office, health insurance, licensing/visas and more) plus AED 250K cash through a SAFE, if they set up a team in Abu Dhabi. Cohort 21 starts in September 2027, and the Hub71+ AI track adds compute and partners such as AWS, NVIDIA, Google for Startups and MBZUAI.
eligibility: Best suited to pre-seed to Series A startups from any country; Indian startups are regularly selected
At least one founder must commit to relocating long-term and building a team in Abu Dhabi
Complete application form plus a PDF pitch deck covering problem, solution, market, traction, funds raised, team and Abu Dhabi plans
For the Hub71+ AI track, AI must be core to the product
benefits: AED 250K flexible in-kind incentives (office, housing, health insurance, licence/visa, growth marketing)
AED 250K cash via SAFE note, plus up to AED 250K more for high performers after one year
Access to Hub71's network of corporate, government and capital partners
items.note: Cohort 21 cut-off is February 2027 (no exact day published). Later applications roll into the next cohort, so intake never closes. Expect a response within about 3 months; pre-deadline applications are reviewed by April 2027. Four-round selection ending with a committee. Cash is equity-linked (SAFE), and relocation is mandatory.

items.title: Thiel Fellowship
items.summary: A two-year, no-equity grant of $250,000 for young founders and builders who skip or leave university to work full time on a company, research project or other venture. Fellows are based in many countries and don't have to move to San Francisco.
eligibility: Aged 22 or younger
No university degree; current students may apply but must drop out to accept
Individuals worldwide can apply (fellows are based in multiple countries)
Working on an ambitious company, project or invention full time
benefits: $250,000 paid over two years, with no equity taken
Access to the Thiel Fellowship founder network and mentors
items.note: Applications are reviewed year-round through the portal at thielfellowship.my.site.com/apply/s/. Questions go to the fellowship team by email. The catch: you must leave formal education to take the award.
